526247|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR89.2 crores with net profit up 78%, but FY26 revenue fell 7% to INR388.3 crores; FY27 guided at INR600-700 crores.
526247|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 20% YoY to INR89.2 crores, with EBIT up 35% to INR9.6 crores (10.8% margin) and PAT up 78% to INR6.6 crores. For full FY26, revenue fell 7% to INR388.3 crores as FY25's high-value chaffs and flares emergency orders were not repeated, while EBIT rose 42% to INR69.3 crores (17.8% margin) and PAT rose 61% to INR45.8 crores, helped by one-off other income. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR600-700 crores and EBIT margin to 15-20%, with the order book at a record INR1,569 crores. Execution remains the central concern: raw material shortages (MIL, DRDO alternate materials), the Katepally plant accident, and pending free-issue material from BDL and DRDO all delayed deliveries.

segments.commentary: INR1,491 crores, about 95% of the INR1,569 crore order book. Q4 Defense & Space revenue was INR67.7 crores, 76% of quarterly revenue.

segments.commentary: INR31 crores, about 2% of the order book.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target INR600-700 crores, versus INR388.3 crores in FY26 (about 50-80% growth). Management said FY27 would be 'commensurate' with the prior year's growth and that the target is 'to try our best'.
FY27 EBIT margin expected at 15-20%, versus 17.8% in FY26.
FY27 export revenue expected at about INR200 crores, with domestic about INR500 crores; management said quarterly phasing will vary.
Of the INR430 crore order won in October 2025, about two-thirds is expected to be executed by end-FY27 and one-third in FY28.

Katepally large rocket motor facility: commissioning targeted by September 2026, with production from November 2026. Broader Katepally RDX/HMX expansion may slip to Q3 FY27, with qualification taking 1-2 months more.
Andhra Pradesh 400-acre defense facility: land price still under negotiation; management expects commissioning 1-1.5 years after the price is finalised.
FY27 capex total of about INR32 crores (INR60 crores less INR28 crores spent in FY26), per management's reconfirmation of earlier guidance.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR28 crores. The FY26-27 plan was INR60 crores in total, comprising Katepally expansion and PDK, which the analyst read as INR45 crores and INR15 crores. Management said the PDK flare plant was already productionised in FY25, with mixers, storage and magazines still under construction.
Katepally: the RDX and HMX expansion is ongoing and not complete. A large planetary mixer and balancing equipment are in progress, and some items are expected to be capitalised by end-Q1 FY27.

Katepally rocket motor facility (large motors for ISRO and DRDO strategic systems) was hit by an accident. Equipment is in fabrication and the building is under construction, with commissioning targeted for September 2026.
Peddakandukur flares plant: rebuilt after an accident about 1.5 years ago, recommissioned, and now producing in-house. Import dependence for flare components has reduced.

Odisha: the first land parcel was rejected and the state government is proposing new parcels. Management is in a video conference with Odisha officials. The three-phase plan has its second and third phases 4-5 years out.

Output is about 50 motors per month across LRSAM, MRSAM and Astra (per management's answer on domestic deliveries). About 40 motors were delivered to domestic customers in the current status described.
demand_pricing: Exports are about 54% of the order book and domestic about 46%. Management said export licences are held for most export orders, and that the INR400 crores of export orders still pending are development orders where invoicing follows milestones.
Newly won INR350.23 crore export order (April 2026) for defence products. Management expects an export licence decision in about 3 months.

A INR18.9 crore order received in February 2026 was cancelled in April because an export licence was not granted. Management said licence rejection risk depends on government policy and the destination country.
Domestic BDL and DRDO orders depend on free-issue materials (FIMs) from those agencies; management said these cannot be executed without them.

Management said alternate raw materials for land mines, loitering munitions and medium-calibre ammunition are in DRDO trials. MIL, the high-explosive supplier, could not meet requirements. Management expects approval within 1-2 months.

Pipeline: QRSAM is not included in the estimates. Some chaffs and flares orders are at negotiation stage and some RFPs are pending. Management expects the order book to stay at about INR1,000 crores-plus after current execution.
Other income: management said the Q4 and FY26 increase came from supplier discounts on delayed deliveries, paid in two parts, and that it is non-recurring.

qa_highlights.question: What growth and margin is targeted for FY27 given fewer emergency orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue target INR600-700 crores and EBIT margin 15-20%. Drivers are land mines, drone and loitering munition payloads, and medium-calibre ammunition, where alternate raw materials have been accepted.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR500 crore guidance from February missed (about INR390 crores delivered)?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material shortages: MIL could not supply inputs for mines, loitering munitions and flares. Alternate materials are in DRDO trials, with production expected once approved in 1-2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Katepally capex on track, and when does it finish?
qa_highlights.answer: Some items to be capitalised by end-Q1 FY27. Full completion may slip to Q3 FY27 because plant and product qualification takes another 1-2 months after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export/domestic split of the order book, and how much export licence risk exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 54% and domestic about 46%. Management said licence approval depends on government policy and the country; the INR18.9 crore cancelled order shows the risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pending order book is stuck, and why?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic orders depend on free-issue materials from BDL and DRDO; about 40 motors delivered recently. Development-stage export orders are being executed against milestones.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the INR430 crore October 2025 order will be executed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution has just started. About two-thirds is expected by end-FY27, with one-third in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Jagdalpur O&M contract lost, and is ISRO renewal possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagdalpur was lost in bidding because costs had risen. ISRO contract has about 2.5 years left, and renewal will be bid when the RFP is issued.

qa_highlights.question: Are there chances of similar accidents, and what mitigations are in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to automation, remote operations and safety control equipment in new plants. The Katepally rocket motor facility is due for commissioning in September 2026.

risks_watch: Execution: FY26 revenue fell 7% and FY27 guidance of INR600-700 crores needs about 50-80% growth. Delivery depends on free-issue material, raw material approvals (DRDO trials) and the Katepally expansion schedule.
Export licence risk: an INR18.9 crore order was cancelled in April 2026 for lack of an export licence, and the INR350 crore export order is awaiting one (expected in about 3 months).
Pending LD (liquidated damages) reversal: about INR30 crores claim pending with MOD, and final flares supply is expected in Q1 FY27.
Other income: FY26 other income of INR42 crores was one-off, which flatters reported PAT and margins. Core margins may be lower than the 17.8% EBIT headline.
Odisha and Andhra Pradesh expansion timelines are uncertain: Odisha phases 2-3 are 4-5 years out, and the Andhra Pradesh land price is still being negotiated.
The ISRO contract (about INR18 crores per year) has about 2.5 years left, and the Jagdalpur O&M contract was lost in bidding.

526247|2026-06.headline: Premier Explosives Q1 FY27 revenue fell 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore, EBIT margin 4.7%, order book INR1,393 crore (94% defence).
526247|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore as dispatches and project execution slipped, mainly on export deliveries held up by maritime disruption and imported countermeasure components. EBIT fell 80% YoY to INR4.8 crore (4.7% margin) and PAT fell 80% to INR3 crore (3% margin), with raw material costs squeezing margins. Management said the export licence backlog is largely cleared and expects the delayed execution to complete in Q2 and Q3. Order book stands at INR1,393 crore, and FY27 revenue target is retained at about INR600 crore. Apollo Micro Systems' acquisition of promoter stake was discussed, with synergy details deferred to next quarter.

segments.name: Defence and Space
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 35% YoY per analyst question; management attributed delays to export licences and component imports, not customer acceptance. Defence is 94% of the order book.

segments.name: Industrial explosives / bulk
segments.commentary: About 6% of order book. Singareni execution of about INR25-30 crore remains for FY27; margins described as very thin, with some contracts negative. Coal India work withdrawn.

segments.name: Services (O&M)
segments.commentary: INR42 crore of order book (3%), no separate commentary on quarterly performance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target retained at about INR600 crore (analyst-reported INR600-700 crore earlier); management said Q1 revenue of about INR103 crore leaves 9 months to deliver INR500-600 crore.
EBITDA margin target of 15-20% for the year, reiterated; management said the gap in Q1 would be made up in coming quarters.
FY27 order inflow expected at INR200-300 crore; management said run rate of INR1,000 crore-plus per year over the next two years.
Export execution targeted at INR150-200 crore in Q2 FY27, with prior-quarter export backlogs expected to clear in the quarter.
Order of INR430 crore (Oct 2025) to be fully executed in FY27 per management, versus earlier guidance of about two-thirds; Q1 execution was about INR21 crore.
Other expenses run-rate of INR9-10 crore per quarter cited as sustainable.
Katepally RDX/HMX water trials expected in September 2026 (about one month); mixing plant dummy trials expected by end September after imported mixer components are airlifted.
capex_capacity: Katepally: RDX and HMX plant integration and erection almost complete; water trials expected September 2026, lasting about one month before production.
Katepally mixing plant: 2.5 tonne planetary mixer installed; imported components delayed by shipping, now being airlifted; dummy trials targeted end-September 2026.
Andhra Pradesh expansion: land pricing unresolved; company has asked the state government to revise price. Management said Apollo would continue the expansion, with a decision after presentation.
Flares produced in own plant; production has started on the July 2023 flares order, with backlog of about INR75 crore to complete in 4-5 months. Chaff payload depends on imports, now executed.
Drones: company builds payloads and partners with drone makers as a partner, not a standalone supplier.
demand_pricing: Export licences: several received in the past week, with some in pipeline; material moving out of factories. Export of INR150-200 crore targeted in Q2.

INR350 crore international defence order (April 2026): export licence still in process; management said licence processing takes at least 3-4 months after importing-country import licence; some dispatches expected in the last quarter of the year.
Bulk explosives: pricing tied to raw material costs; more than 40 players in the segment; management declined to predict FY28.
RDX/HMX: international demand good, but licences difficult; management said war-driven demand has lifted prices for now.
Alternate raw material for mines/loitering munitions under DRDO, ARDE and HEMRL testing; management expects about 6 more months.
Naval opportunity linked to Apollo association; potential to be clearer by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall from INR20 crore to INR11 crore, and is INR11 crore sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier quarters had expected credit loss provisions and forex losses that did not recur; a sustainable run rate of about INR9-10 crore per quarter was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin improve from the 35% level, and what is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will improve as the product mix and dispatches improve; it reiterated the 15-20% EBITDA target and did not quantify a gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the roughly INR400 crore of export licences, and what export revenue is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Several licences received in the past week, with material moving; INR150-200 crore of export is targeted in Q2, and prior-quarter export backlogs expected to clear this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR430 crore October 2025 order on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 execution was about INR21 crore, the order will be fully executed in FY27 (not two-thirds), and capacity is available with chaff imports already executed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Defence revenue fall 35%, and was it procurement or acceptance delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to export licence and component import delays, and said customer procurement and acceptance were not a cause; completion expected in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook if raw material prices normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material prices are not normalising yet; contracts already signed must be executed first, then prices will be raised. The 15-20% EBITDA target is for this financial year.

risks_watch: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to about 6% (per analyst calculation) from about 15% in the prior year, with raw material cost and under-absorption cited; recovery to 15-20% depends on contracts and price pass-through.
FY27 revenue of INR600 crore needs INR500-600 crore in 9 months after INR103 crore in Q1; Chaff imports remain dependent on conditions abroad.

key_quotes: Encouragingly, we believe that many of these external headwinds are gradually easing as supply chain stabilize and execution improves, we expect a stronger operational performance and better revenue conversion in the coming quarters.

526247|2026-09.headline: Premier Explosives Q2 FY27 revenue rose 92% YoY to Rs 1,452.8 mn and EBITDA rose 161% YoY to Rs 172.3 mn, with order book at Rs 16,420 mn.
526247|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations recovered sharply from a weak Q1 that was hit by dispatch and project delays linked to global headwinds and supply chain disruptions. EBITDA margin widened to 11.9% from 8.7% a year earlier and 5.7% in Q1. H1 FY27 profitability fell year on year, with EBITDA down 15.9% and PAT down 54.8%. Management said the order book stood at Rs 16,420 mn as of October 2026, about 96% defense. Q&A was dominated by export licence delays, the RDX/HMX capacity ramp, margin pressure, and the Apollo Micro Systems transaction.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the revenue recovery momentum to continue; H2 revenue of about Rs 300 cr was implied by an analyst and not contradicted, based on the countermeasures order balance of about Rs 270 cr expected to complete before March 2027.
Kakinada-type RDX/HMX plant: commercial production targeted by mid-to-end December 2026; initial Q4 FY27 output around 30 tonnes with about Rs 20 cr revenue potential.
FY28 RDX/HMX target of about 300 tonnes, at a blended realisation of USD 60-80 per tonne, with 50-60% consumed internally; subject to export licences.
Export licence for the Apr-2026 LV export order (~Rs 50 cr) expected 'next month', but timing is not in management's control.
Shafts and flares expected to contribute about Rs 200 cr of revenue in FY27 based on current orders.
capex_capacity: RDX/HMX capacity being raised from 100 tpa to 600 tpa; commissioning targeted by the end of this financial year.
H1 FY27 capex was about Rs 11 cr against an earlier plan of about Rs 32 cr for FY27; the shortfall is expected to be spent in H2 on the RDX/HMX project and logistics.
Mine programme: Nippon Mines order in hand; Roshi and Ulka are in qualification. Order size mentioned as more than Rs 2 lakh pieces (transcript unclear); value not disclosed.
Drone payloads are in armed forces qualification and currently supplied on trial basis in small quantities; volume not quantified.
40 mm grenade ammunition: stalled, dependent on imported propellants and primers from MIL, which are unavailable.
No plans to set up 155 mm artillery shell facility.
demand_pricing: Countermeasures order (Jul 2023, ~Rs 75 cr): delivery period extension from the government expected in the current quarter; about Rs 30 cr receivable pending on this order.
Countermeasures order (Oct 2025, Rs 430 cr): about Rs 110 cr executed by H1; balance about Rs 270 cr expected to complete before March 2027.
Export orders: licence process takes 3-4 months after buyer end-user certificates are submitted to MoD and DGTR (transcribed as DVP); applications are made order by order, not product by product.
RDX/HMX international prices described as fluid; demand exceeds supply in both domestic and export markets.

Gross margin on defense mixture supply has declined from about 42% in FY26 (as stated by analyst) to lower levels, attributed to a long-term 10-11 year fixed-price contract, imported Flare components after an accident at the Flare plant last year, and supply chain delays. Management said commercial-segment margins should target at least 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Has the delivery period extension on the Jul 2023 countermeasures order (Rs 75 cr) been received, and when will the balance be completed?
qa_highlights.answer: Extension expected this quarter; supplies are continuing. Completion about three months after extension. About Rs 30 cr receivable pending.

qa_highlights.question: When will the export licence for the Apr-2026 LV export order (~Rs 50 cr) be received?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is in final stages and could come next month, but declined to give a precise timeline, saying it depends on government and committee approval.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be new bulk explosives orders from Singareni or Coal India subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Singareni extended the existing contract and supplies continue; expected about Rs 80 cr of bulk explosives revenue this year. Future growth depends on Singareni's new RFP.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RDX/HMX revenue potential in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 300 tonnes output at USD 60-80 per tonne blended realisation, with 50-60% consumed internally. Depends on export licences.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Apollo acquisition expected to change governance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said governance is expected to remain the same for now and did not comment further.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AP land status?
qa_highlights.answer: The state government has formulated a defense and ammunition industry policy; the company selected one of four options. A board reconstitution is expected by December 2026 in connection with the Apollo transaction.

risks_watch: Export licence timelines (3-4 months per order after end-user documents) are outside management control and have delayed revenue.
Gross margin compression from fixed-price long-term contracts, imported components and supply chain delays.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided shafts/flares about Rs 200 cr, bulk explosives about Rs 80 cr and countermeasures balance about Rs 270 cr for FY27, but H1 PAT fell 54.8% and export licence timing is uncontrolled, so no upward revision is evident.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Export licence for the Apr-2026 LV order (~Rs 50 cr) is pending with no firm timeline, the 40 mm ammunition programme is stalled on unavailable MIL propellants, and the RDX/HMX ramp starts only from December 2026.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Drone payloads are in armed forces qualification on trial supply with volume unquantified, and RDX/HMX output starts at about 30 tonnes in Q4 FY27; the 40 mm grenade programme is stalled.

rows.label: Countermeasures order balance execution
rows.why: About Rs 270 cr of the Rs 430 cr Oct 2025 countermeasures order is expected to complete before March 2027, after about Rs 110 cr executed in H1 FY27.

rows.label: Export RDX/HMX and LV export licences
rows.why: Apr-2026 LV export order (~Rs 50 cr) licence is in final stages and could come next month, but management declined a precise timeline; FY28 RDX/HMX target of about 300 tonnes at USD 60-80 per tonne depends on licences.

rows.label: Apollo Micro Systems stake and board reconstitution
rows.why: Apollo is acquiring an additional 41.33% stake with board reconstitution expected by December 2026, though management said governance will remain the same for now.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q2 recovery, order book and RDX/HMX commissioning, but cautious and evasive on export licence timing, order-level margins and product-level revenue potential; analysts probed licence delays, the RDX/HMX ramp, margin pressure and the Apollo transaction.

526263|2026-03.headline: Mold-Tek Q4 FY26 PAT turned to INR 2.28 crore from a loss, but FY26 PAT fell 17% to INR 10 crore on a INR 4 crore FX MTM hit.
526263|2026-03.overview: Management reported a Q4 FY26 profit of INR 2.28 crore versus a loss of about INR 1.6 crore a year earlier, despite a roughly INR 4 crore MTM loss from rupee depreciation on forward contracts. Full-year PAT was about INR 10 crore against INR 12.16 crore in FY25, with management citing EBITDA of about INR 20 crore standalone (INR 19.64 crore consolidated) against INR 23 crore a year earlier. Beryl, acquired in November 2025, contributed five months of revenue, and the MES automobile (BIW) team was cut from about 160 to 60 people by end-March. Management reiterated plans to move into structural design and targets of INR 250 crore revenue and 15% EBITDA margin for FY27. Analyst questions were pointed on EBITDA definition, the cancelled preferential issue, receivables and hedging, and several figures were disputed or left for follow-up with the CFO.

segments.name: Civil / Structural (steel detailing and design, India-based, US clients)
segments.commentary: Work on hand grew from about $4 million at start of FY26 to about $5 million at end-March 2026, which management described as growth of about 60-70% versus $2.84 million in June 2024. Structural design is about 10% of civil revenue, versus nearly 0% three to four years ago. Management targets 30-40% of revenue from design in three to four years.

segments.name: MES (Mechanical Engineering Services) - BIW automobile
segments.commentary: Team cut from about 160 to 60 people by end-March; the team was closed from April 1. The segment lost about INR 7-8 crore a year and about INR 1.7-1.9 crore in Q4 FY26. Work on hand fell from about $0.5 million in Q1 to about $0.25 million.

segments.name: MES - Poles, towers and substation (US)
segments.commentary: Team grew from 45-50 to about 80 people. FY26 revenue was about $0.8 million; management expects FY27 to cross $1.5-2 million. Around 80-90% of this work comes from the USA.

segments.name: Beryl (US residential structural design, inspection and permitting; acquired Nov 2025)
segments.commentary: Revenue mix about 80% permitting/inspection and 20% design. Team of about 40 in Tampa with no resignations in five months. Management guided Beryl margin at 8-10% for FY27 and said it can grow to about $5-7 million with India design support.

segments.name: PEMB (Pre-Engineering Metal Buildings)
segments.commentary: Now about 5% of revenue, down from being the core business before 2010.

segments.name: New MSA with Danieli Corus (Delhi, MES manpower)
segments.commentary: Mandate for 20 people; 3 fulfilled so far. Contract period 1-3 years, potential about $0.5 million per annum within a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR 250 crore, with management saying INR 240 crore is 'easily feasible' from the Q4 run-rate of INR 59 crore (times four).
EBITDA margin to move from about 11% to at least 15%.
Standalone engineering business (MES plus civil from India) expected to grow at least 15-20%, with EBITDA margin in the 15-16% region.
MES cost cut expected to add about INR 7-8 crore back to profitability; productivity target improvement of at least 20% in FY27 (10-15% gain claimed in April).
Nashik office move expected to save about INR 2-2.5 crore per year from FY28; building targeted to be ready by end of FY27.
Hedging policy to be limited to 25-50% of turnover (previously up to 100%); operational EBITDA to be reported separately from MTM gains and losses from FY27.
Salary hike of 8.5-9% provided in Q4 for Indian teams; Beryl not yet covered.
capex_capacity: Team of 40-45 structural designers in India plus 2-3 in the USA; a 6-member Indian team was created for Beryl, with a plan for a 15-20 person India team, targeted by Q4 FY27.
Nashik owned building site acquired a couple of years ago; municipal approvals expected by end of May, ground work in June, completion by end FY27.
Management is in talks for an acquisition of a high-rise steel structural design company; one target is near the Atlanta office. No deal concluded.
Two PEs (professional engineers) certified in more than 20 US states; PE support needed for full member design.
demand_pricing: Civil work on hand up to about $5 million at end-March 2026, against about $4 million at start of the year (per Q4 opening remarks); Q&A figure of $2.5 million at start of year.
Pricing: projects quoted on a fixed-price basis at about $30/hour in India, with 2-3% negotiation; structural design rates about $70-80 per hour versus $25-30 for detailing.
Trade uncertainty between the US and India has stalled Interarch and Mold-Tek building orders in the US; no revenue progress from Interarch or Affordable Robotic Partnership.
BIW automobile demand fell as EV adoption and new model launches slowed; European work was over 50% of MES, while poles and towers are 80-90% US.
Beryl order book estimated at $0.2-0.3 million at any time, maximum about $0.5 million (per management; to be checked).

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 INR 250 crore revenue and 15% EBITDA margin realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 240 crore is easily feasible from Q4 revenue of INR 59 crore annualised, and that margin should rise from 11% to at least 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 2.9 lakh preferential issue at INR 164 cancelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the investor did not transfer funds because the share price had fallen to about INR 130, so the issue lapsed on 30 April against a 31 May deadline. The issue was independent of the Beryl stake purchase. About 30% of acquisition money is held as a three-year retention guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation hit P&L when costs are mainly wages, and what is the hedging policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Forwards booked at INR 85-92 led to about INR 4.9 crore MTM loss in Q4 as rupee moved to about INR 95. Management is cutting hedge cover to 25-50% of turnover and will show MTM separately from operational EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables doubled and revenue rose only about 40%; is the standalone business weakening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 turnover rose 81% YoY, that the rise in debtors reflects this growth, and that acquisitions are strategic rather than a response to weakness. It cited zero debt and INR 25-30 crore of deposits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MES loss and when does it end?
qa_highlights.answer: The MES loss was about INR 1.7-1.9 crore in Q4 and about INR 7-8 crore a year; management said the team was closed from 1 April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What were Beryl's revenue and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Beryl did INR 22.9 crore in the five months since acquisition, including INR 11 crore in Q4 with a loss of about INR 70 lakh. Management said Beryl's seasonal Q4 is typically weak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Danieli Corus MSA and its revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: A manpower MSA in MES with a mandate for 20 people (3 deployed so far), a contract period of 1-3 years, and potential of about $0.5 million per year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY26 Florida SB 4-D inspection tailwind at Beryl ending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first inspection phase is complete and payments received; the second design phase was delayed by a government shutdown and is now restarting, so the tailwind is mid-cycle.

qa_highlights.question: What is the threat from AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI has a limited role in design and detailing, may cut headcount by 5-10% through checking tasks, and that back charges are zero.

526263|2026-06.headline: Mold-Tek Q1 FY27 profit rose about 12x YoY with EBITDA margin near 19-23%, though Beryl (US) still contributes nothing to bottom line.
526263|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 profitability was roughly 4x Q4 and 12x Q1 last year, driven by MES downsizing, lower other expenses (including absence of prior-quarter MTM losses) and automation. Beryl, the US residential permitting acquisition, was around break-even and is guided to break even in Q2 and contribute positively from Q3. Civil and structural work on hand was about $4.5 million versus $3.5-3.7 million a year earlier, and MES work on hand was about $1.15 million. Management reiterated FY27 ex-Beryl revenue of Rs 240-250 crore (about Rs 61 crore achieved in Q1) and an indicative Rs 300-350 crore for FY28 together with a structural engineering acquisition.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~15% guided earlier; FY26 EBITDA margin ~11% per management

financial_highlights.value: ~12x Q1 FY26 (Q1 FY26 PAT Rs 78 lakh)

segments.commentary: Work on hand about $4.5 million vs $3.5-3.7 million a year ago; project sizes $20k-$500k, lasting 3-12 months. Management treats work on hand as the key leading indicator.

segments.name: MES (Mechanical, Electrical, Structural)
segments.commentary: Work on hand about $1.15 million, flat YoY. Team cut from 125-130 to 50-60 people; EV/automobile design kept at small scale. Power T&D and substation design (poles, towers) now the focus, with a new US power distribution contract (~$1 million per annum, team ramping to 20 by Oct-Nov).

segments.name: Beryl (US residential permitting, Florida; Georgia entry)
segments.commentary: Not yet contributing to bottom line; around break-even, with a marginal loss of $5-10k over 8 months post-acquisition. Received a ~$1 million master purchase order from Hillsborough County; Georgia (Atlanta) listing started.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue ex-Beryl of Rs 240-250 crore reiterated; management says similar Q2 run-rate supports this.
EBITDA margin expected to stay at least 20%, possibly 20-23%, for the current year (management's wording); PAT margin target 15-16% with Beryl adding upside.

US data-center-linked power T&D opportunity sized at $5-10 million per annum for Mold-Tek; sector ~$0.5-1 billion.
capex_capacity: MES team cut to 50-60 people from 125-130 a year ago; doubling the power/T&D design team in the last couple of months.
Indian design team for Beryl being built (6-8 people, target 15-20 by Oct-Nov); one PE relocating to Florida from October subject to L1 visa.

Proposed acquisition of a US structural engineering firm (~15 engineers, half PEs/SEs); talks ongoing, CEO to visit US from 16 Aug, chairman late September; decision targeted October and closing possibly within calendar 2026.
Atlanta office (5-6 staff) supports Beryl's Georgia entry; Beryl previously had 38 people at acquisition, lost 2 design staff.
demand_pricing: Civil work on hand $4.5 million (vs $3.7 million last year per one answer; $3.5 million per another), with both existing and new clients.
Power/T&D: new MSA with a US power distribution client; ~10 people billed from July, 20 by Oct-Nov.
Management says Indian rates are very low versus US; focus remains on US work.
Consulting fee model: management aims to charge 2-3% of project cost (vs hourly) once a design firm is integrated.

Beryl's residential/government revenue hit by US government funding shutdown in Jan-May; Florida residential permits reportedly down ~10% YoY (raised by analyst, management attributed partly to demand).

qa_highlights.question: What was the EBITDA per barrel in Q1 and what cost savings are sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Beryl was about break-even; per-barrel EBITDA not given. Savings came from MES downsizing, cut software costs and absence of prior-quarter MTM losses; management called automation and incentive changes long-term.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin jump to 19% versus 15% guidance and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited reduced automobile engineering costs, automation and productivity incentives visible for 3-5 months, and a work-on-hand build; described these as long-term, not one-time.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Beryl promoter subscribe to warrants?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6-month window lapsed in April when the 6-month average price (~Rs 165) exceeded market (~Rs 130); promoter did not subscribe and management will not press.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $5-10 million power opportunity sector-wide or company-specific?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-specific opportunity of $5-10 million per annum; sector is ~$0.5-1 billion, with ~$100 million of substation design and detailing outsourced from US.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Indicative Rs 300-350 crore target for FY28 along with a structural engineering acquisition; management said it cannot predict beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: What caused Beryl's sales slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly demand (US government funding shutdown for 4-5 months, affecting government-funded work Jan-May) and partly internal design team disruption after losing 2 design staff in November.

526263|2026-09.headline: Mold-Tek H1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose to INR 18.62 crore, about 4.7x the prior-year H1, with standalone Q2 PAT of INR 10.16 crore.
526263|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong Q2 FY27 numbers: standalone Q2 turnover of INR 46.64 crore (up 25% YoY) and PAT of INR 10.16 crore versus INR 3.15 crore a year earlier, with standalone H1 PAT of about INR 20 crore. Consolidated H1 PAT was INR 18.62 crore against INR 10 crore for full FY26. Management attributed the gains to product mix, operational efficiency, and higher-value engineering services in poles and towers and structural steel detailing. The BIW segment has been cut sharply, and the Beryl acquisition is still loss-making (about USD 25,000 loss in Q2) with breakeven targeted for Q3.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 3.15 crore in Q2 FY26 (more than 3x)
vs gain of INR 1.5 crore in Q1

financial_highlights.value: Manpower contribution INR 5,220 per head (Q2) vs INR 4,500 in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Structural steel detailing and civil structural work (standalone)
segments.commentary: Management said about 75-80% of revenue comes from structural steel detailing and related areas, roughly USD 4.4-5.3 million of H1 work (about 80-82%). Connection design is tracking toward about USD 1 million this year.

segments.name: Poles, towers and power distribution (utility fixed teams, MAS)
segments.commentary: Team grew from 30-40 people last year to 70-75 now, with a target of 120 by March 2027 against fixed-team demand of 110-125. Management said there is a severe shortage of talent in this skill set.

segments.name: BIW / automotive (MES)
segments.commentary: Revenue from MES automobile services has fallen to about USD 100,000 in the quarter. BIW headcount was cut from 150-160 to about 50, with a further 5-10 possible reduction and 20-25 people being retrained.

segments.name: Beryl (US subsidiary, acquired about 9-10 months ago)
segments.commentary: Still loss-making, with a loss of about USD 25,000 in Q2 versus USD 70,000-75,000 in Q1. A USD 1 million Hillsborough County design order was received in October, and breakeven is targeted for Q3.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated top-line growth of at least 18-20% and standalone growth of about 20-25% over the next 12-18 months, subject to dollar movements.
Management expects a further 15% productivity gain without a large headcount increase, which could take revenue per employee to about USD 35,000 per year.
Beryl expected to turn positive in Q3 FY27 (breakeven) and to contribute meaningfully in FY28.
Poles and towers growth expected from Q3 or Q4, with the ramp-up of fixed teams to 120 by March 2027.
Civil and land development work with a US client expected to become sizable from January-February 2027; an MOU is already signed.
Management gave no quantitative FY28 margin guidance. It said the company should stay on a positive track for the next one to two years.
capex_capacity: Utility fixed-team headcount is planned to rise from about 70-75 to 120 by March 2027. Some 40-45 people are in training, and the MSA is for 25 people, with 10-15 currently offered.
BIW headcount is being reduced to a nominal size, with outsourcing of residual work to small players planned.
Beryl's design team is centred on six engineers, with a five-person team in Hyderabad supporting a design head based in Tampa.
Automation and tooling are being introduced to lift output and quality. Management said no large recruitment is needed and that hiring will be project-driven.
Management is open to an acquisition of a US structural design firm but is not satisfied with the current candidate and is considering other targets. No decision has been made.
demand_pricing: Work on hand fell to about USD 4.2 million from USD 4.5 million in Q1, but October brought record bookings and the level is now above end-June.
Data centre engineering: 5-6 projects completed over the past 1-2 years, with 2-3 on hand now. Each project is about USD 300-500k.
Management said US outsourcing of core civil and mechanical engineering will keep growing given local engineer shortages.
Management said structural design commands higher hourly rates than detailing, and expects residential, architectural and civil work to carry much higher fees than steel detailing.
The rupee was stabilising around USD 95 per dollar, which management expects to yield forex gains in Q3 if it holds.

526299|2026-03.headline: Mphasis Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7.1% YoY in constant currency to $463 Mn, with record FY26 net new TCV of $2.1 Bn (up 68%).

526371|2026-03.headline: NMDC guides FY27 production to 60 million tonnes and FY27 capex to about INR6,000 crore, with Q1 FY27 output up about 15% YoY.
526371|2026-03.overview: NMDC reported FY26 production above 50 million tonnes and an 11% PAT rise despite sluggish prices, with management citing a record capex of about INR3,300 crore. Management guided FY27 production to 60 million tonnes, with the first two months of Q1 FY27 about 15% higher YoY at roughly 10 million tonnes. New iron ore (Deposit 4, Deposit 13) and coal (Tokisud, Rohne) assets are being commissioned, and a INR3,000 crore blending yard at Vizag is sanctioned. The EBITDA margin was 33% group-level, down from 42%, due to a one-time HR coil trading arrangement with NMDC Steel; standalone iron ore EBITDA was stated at 42%.

segments.name: Iron ore (NMDC standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone EBITDA margin at 42%, with FY27 guided at 42-43%. Kirandul FY26 about 21 million tonnes (to ~30 million by decade-end); Bacheli about 18-19 million tonnes (to ~35 million).

segments.name: NMDC Steel (NSL)
segments.commentary: NSL has turned profitable; the HR coil trading in the last quarter was a one-time cash-flow support and is not expected in Q1 FY27. NSL dues are being recovered at about INR100 crore per month, with full liquidation in 16-18 months (pre-demerger dues about INR2,500 crore, now about INR1,800 crore).

segments.name: Coal
segments.commentary: Tokisud (2.3 million tonnes peak, thermal, opened) targets 0.75-1 million tonnes in FY27 from Q2; Rohne (8 million tonnes peak coking coal) opens around end-Q3 FY27 with no FY27 production. Management expects INR500-600 crore revenue per 1 million tonnes at G10 grade, at 30-40% EBITDA (approximate).

segments.name: Pellets (KIOCL)
segments.commentary: KIOCL 3 million tonne job-work plant: FY26 about 2.4 million tonnes; FY27 target 3-3.3 million tonnes. Pellet grade achieved 66.5% Fe; targeting 67% DR-grade with a $20-30/t premium.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at 60 million tonnes including NSL, built from Deposit 14 (+1 mt), NMZ (+1 mt), Kumaraswamy (+~3.3 mt), Deposit 5 (+2 mt to 12 mt), plus Deposit 4 (~1 mt) and Deposit 13 (~0.5 mt).
Deposit 4 expected to start commercial mining in Q2 FY27: about 1 mt in FY27, 2 mt in FY28, and 7 mt peak rated capacity after 1.5-2 more years.
Deposit 13 start targeted around Q2 FY27 after pending clearances: under 0.5 mt in FY27, about 2 mt next year, 10 mt initial peak rising to 20-21 mt in 4-5 years.
Capex guidance: about INR6,000 crore in FY27 (range INR6,000-7,000 crore); INR7,000-10,000 crore per year over the next 2-3 years; INR40,000-50,000 crore over 3 years to reach 100 mt.
Overseas critical mineral and mineral asset acquisitions: INR2,000-3,000 crore expected in FY27; a couple of overseas assets targeted this year.
Management reiterated a 100 million tonne target by end of decade and said the 60 mt FY27 guidance is achievable without the railway doubling, but 100 mt requires it.
No immediate plans to leverage the balance sheet; internal accruals expected to fund capex and acquisitions, with debt possible late FY27 only for large global acquisitions.
Iron ore prices expected to stay range-bound in FY27; monthly price calls to be taken.
capex_capacity: Railway: 131 km doubling; two sections remaining, one by end of June 2026 and the Bhansi-Bacheli section by December 2026; evacuation capacity to rise from 28-30 mt to ~40 mt, with 60 mt+ after doubling beyond Jagdalpur.
Slurry pipeline (15 mt, Bacheli to Nagarnar), Nagarnar pellet plant and Bacheli grinding mill in pre-commissioning; commissioning expected by end-June or mid-July 2026.
EC capacity 64.8 mt vs CTO ~55.4 mt; CTO enhancement sought in three places to ~58.8 mt. All mines reached EC capacity as of 1 April 2026 (Deposit 5 the exception in FY26).
Deposit 5 downhill conveyor and bottleneck fix due June-July 2026, enabling 12 mt. New infrastructure at Deposit 14, NMZ, 11 and 11C takes about 1.5 years, adding 5-6 mt.
INR3,000 crore blending yard at Vizag (board sanctioned, ~2-2.5 year build); Vizag land parcel ~1,100 acres; pellet plant at Vizag on drawing board, pending slurry pipeline route decision.
Expansion works (~INR15,000-20,000 crore worth of major tenders) expected to be awarded by end-June or July 2026.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is not a constraint even at 100 mt, citing JSW, AMNS (10 mt plant near Vizag, 17 mt total), JSPL and NSL expansions; NMDC's phosphorus content of 0.05% is a claimed differentiator.

Iron ore prices expected range-bound in Q1 FY27 after steel prices peaked Dec-Feb and stabilised in March-April; the company sets prices monthly, citing international prices, competitor prices and logistics, not a direct steel-price link.
RINL consumes 7-8 mt per year; bills discounted at ~10% premium with a 45-day payment lag; no recourse to NMDC in FY25 or FY26.
Blended/branded iron ore (Vizag) planned as a premium product; exports unattractive given 30% export duty, so pellets are preferred for export.
Iron ore realisation slightly down ~2% per an analyst question; no quantified FY27 realisation guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Mine-wise bridge to 60 mt FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit 14 +1 mt, NMZ +1 mt, Kumaraswamy +~3.3 mt (MPAP relief from 8.6 mt), Deposit 5 +2 mt (to 12 mt), totalling ~5.3 mt; plus Deposit 4 (~1 mt) and Deposit 13 (~0.5 mt) gives ~60 mt including NSL.

qa_highlights.question: Coal mine economics and grade?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial volume mostly via auction at prices above CIL FSA; 1 mt is estimated at INR500-600 crore revenue with 30-40% EBITDA. Grade is G10; figures described as very preliminary.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery of NSL and RINL receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: NSL dues cut from ~INR2,500 crore to ~INR1,800 crore; recovery at ~INR100 crore per month, 16-18 months for NSL, about a year and a half to two for the rest. RINL is 100% government-owned, with timing slower but no risk assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and critical minerals spending?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex ~INR6,000 crore (range 6,000-7,000), then INR7,000-10,000 crore per year. Overseas acquisitions INR2,000-3,000 crore in FY27; domestic rare earth via GMDC MoU in Gujarat, no firm profitability guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Can 60 mt be reached without railway doubling?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, 60 mt is achievable without it, but 100 mt is not possible without the doubling completing (Vizag/Bhansi-Bacheli section due December 2026).

qa_highlights.question: Deposit 4, Deposit 13 and Rohne ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit 4 ~1 mt in FY27, 2 mt in FY28, 7 mt peak; Deposit 13 under 0.5 mt FY27, 2 mt next year, 10 mt initially rising to 20-21 mt; Rohne opens around end-Q3 FY27 with no FY27 output and 8 mt peak coking coal.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA guidance and realisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore EBITDA margin to be maintained at 42-43% for FY27; no specific per-tonne realisation or EBITDA-per-tonne figures were given.

Railway doubling completion (December 2026 for Bhansi-Bacheli) is a prerequisite for 100 mt.

526381|2026-03.headline: FY26 PBT crossed INR10 crore at INR10.30 crore (up ~34%), with PAT of INR9.58 crore and a 30% payout dividend of INR0.40 per share.
526381|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 total income from operations up 11.68% YoY to INR96.74 crore, with PBT up nearly 99% to INR3.70 crore and PAT up over 60% to INR2.98 crore. The air freight segment profit rose to INR11.26 crore from INR8.53 crore, and finance cost fell by INR35 lakh to a lower level from INR1.18 crore. segments.name: Air freight logistics

segments.name: Rajpat Logistics Limited (new subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Formed in the December 2025 quarter; management says it is at a nascent stage. It will book trucking for top corporates on an asset-light basis, and management expects it to add about 25% to the INR400 crore revenue base and to earn ROCE above 15%.

526423|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose to INR 18 crore (margin 12.91% vs 0.15%) on revenue of INR 142 crore, while FY26 volume fell 13% to 58,630 MT.
526423|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 recovered sharply from a weak prior year: revenue grew 3% YoY to INR 142 crore and EBITDA reached INR 18 crore versus INR 20 lakh a year earlier, with net profit of about INR 4 crore against a loss of INR 4 crore. For the full year, revenue fell 19% to INR 587 crore and volume fell 13%, attributed to heavy rains in operating areas, but EBITDA rose 23% to INR 35 crore and net profit was INR 1 crore versus a loss of INR 4 crore. Management linked Q4 inventory gains to PVC price volatility from the Middle East conflict, and said capex is on hold for two quarters. Several answers deferred to the CFO, reducing detail on freight, dealers and utilisation.

segments.commentary: Q4 volume 10,288 MT (+12% YoY); FY26 volume 47,638 MT (-11%). Management cites typical margins of 8-10%, varying by season.

segments.name: Building products
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 2,683 MT (+7% YoY); FY26 volume 7,685 MT (-16%). Margins stated at 14-18%, higher than agriculture; management targets substantial growth in FY27 and CPVC expansion.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 606 MT (-65% YoY); FY26 volume 3,307 MT (-29%).

Building products are to be the main FY27 growth driver, with CPVC expansion; OPVC is not on the agenda.

demand_pricing: Demand for agri and building products was hit when the Middle East war pushed raw material and finished goods prices up sharply; management says demand is now back to near normal.
Management says PVC prices are volatile after the Iran-Iraq conflict; Q4 included inventory gains, and the company stocked up in March ahead of the April-June agri season.
The government withdrew import duty on PVC and other polymers until about 1 July; management said there is no anti-dumping duty.
Competition is aggressive with many national players present in MP; branded players are gaining share from unorganised ones.

qa_highlights.answer: Capex is on hold until the first two quarters of FY27 are reviewed. Management said expansion beyond the region is limited for agri but feasible for building materials, and any new capacity will be carefully considered.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the March inventory build is routine, to prepare for the April-June agri season, and gave no figures.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said other expenses mainly comprise freight; the CFO would provide the breakdown offline. No figures were given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Has the building products segment crossed INR 100 crore, and what is the expected contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said building products revenue fell in FY26 due to rationalisation and will see a quantum jump in FY27, but gave no figure for the segment's FY26 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables fall, from INR 48 crore to INR 28 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivables are mostly from institutional customers, which the company cut in Q4 as planned.

526612|2026-03.headline: Blue Dart Q4 FY26 PAT fell to INR 43 crore on revenue of INR 1,533 crore; comparable PBT before exceptional items down about 17% YoY.
526612|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations reached INR 6,141 crore versus INR 5,720 crore in FY25, with full-year PAT of INR 240 crore. Management said FY26 revenue and PBT before the Labour Code exceptional item each grew about 7%. Q4 revenue grew about 8%, but comparable PBT before exceptional items fell about 17%, with no exceptional item in the quarter. Management attributed the margin pressure to a mix shift toward heavier, lower-margin ground shipments, higher local vehicle hiring costs in March, and employee cost investments in sales and quality functions.

segments.commentary: About 60% of FY26 revenue by value; management said air is a transit-time product, not a mode, with about one-third of air load on commercial airlines and two-thirds on own aircraft. E-commerce air growth was described as steady with limited growth.

segments.name: Ground / surface
segments.commentary: About 40% of FY26 revenue by value and the stated growth engine; FY26 surface rate growth was 6.9% per management, and its share has risen from about 30-32% a few quarters ago.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue split 70.3% B2B and 29.7% B2C; Q4 split about 71:29. B2C is described as essentially e-commerce, split 17% air and 12% surface of total revenue.

ATF/fuel impact expected from April 2026 (FY27 Q1) but described as largely neutralized by the fuel surcharge mechanism.

Smaller-weight B2B e-commerce movements (store-to-store, warehouse-to-store) grew faster, and management said surface volume growth was slower than FY25 as customer composition changed.

qa_highlights.question: Is ATF price movement affecting FY27 Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ATF rose from March but the fuel surcharge is set at the start of the month, so no significant Q4 impact; impact from April is largely neutralised by the fuel surcharge mechanism.

qa_highlights.question: Will ground growth lift profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ground costs are largely variable, unlike air where asset investment gives better incremental returns, so ground growth may not drive a dramatic profit increase.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said aircraft engine and maintenance capex of about INR 100-150 crore a year is recurring; standalone capex was INR 120 crore plus ROU assets of about INR 400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a West Asia-related charter opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said charter demand is limited to a few repeat domestic customers and one-off charters; it is not seeing a big new opportunity now.

qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds on own aircraft and one-third on commercial airlines, with about 25 additional airports served only by commercial carriers.

Ground facility ramp-up (Gurugram) and fixed-cost absorption; management said ground is largely variable-cost.
Fuel and ATF pass-through from April 2026; management said it is largely neutralised, but this is untested.
Recurring aircraft maintenance capex of INR 100-150 crore a year affects free cash flow.
Peak-season (H2) cost ramp and local fleet availability, which hit March 2026.

526612|2026-06.headline: Blue Dart Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR1,658 crore (from INR1,442 crore) and PAT reached INR87 crore, driven mainly by yield and fuel surcharge rather than volume.
526612|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR1,658 crore against INR1,442 crore a year earlier, with PAT of INR87 crore. Management attributed growth mainly to pricing: GPI-led increases, targeted repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery after diesel and Brent prices rose from around March–May. Tonnage grew about 7% to 364,430 tons and shipments about 2% to 96.15 million, with air volume up about 2.6% and surface up about 9%. Management declined to quantify yield growth or give forward volume and margin guidance, citing seasonality and H2 resourcing challenges.

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: About 60% of revenue but about 25% of kilos (1:3 air:surface by weight). Volume growth about 2.6%; growth is mainly yield-led. Freighter pallet utilisation 85–90%.

segments.name: Surface / Ground
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue and about 75% of kilos. Volume up about 9%; B2B revenue up about 14%. Management says surface is the faster-growing segment and is approaching air in size.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Revenue up more than 10% YoY. Management says about 50-plus million of the 96.15 million shipments are e-commerce, and Blue Dart holds about 12–13% of outsourced/3PL e-commerce.

segments.name: B2B vs B2C
segments.commentary: Revenue mix about 70% B2B and 30% B2C (plus or minus 2%).

segments.name: BFSI (documents and cards)
segments.commentary: BFSI alone is about 10–15% of total revenue; documents plus cards together, including small parcels, about 25–30%. Management says BFSI is no longer a growing segment.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance. Management said it will not forecast volumes, citing seasonality, but expects Q2 to reflect the full fuel-surcharge increase from May onward.
Typical GPI realisation is about 4–5%, with extra customer-specific corrections on top.

Standalone annualised capex guided at INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Aviation capex is driven by maintenance and engine cycles, with roughly 20–25% of depreciation as ongoing capex.
H2 is expected to bring higher volumes, but resourcing flex will determine margins; management aims for stable, consistent margin improvement.
No major expansion plans; growth is expected to be organic. Possible consolidation and expansion of southern hubs (Bangalore, Chennai) and Mumbai, a few quarters away.
capex_capacity: Two major hubs added in North and a couple of medium-sized hubs in East in the prior period.
Freighter pallet utilisation at 85–90%; aircraft flown mainly at night and scheduled against available load.
Belly cargo is 30–40% of overall load in a typical month, and can reach 70–80% on lower-volume weekends. Blue Dart flies to 8 stations and carries belly cargo at 25–50 other locations.
The two aircraft acquired earlier are back to pre-acquisition pallet utilisation (as of 2024) and are integrated into the network.
demand_pricing: Growth came mainly from pricing: GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge pass-through. Management said yield was 'directionally' the main driver of revenue growth.
Fuel surcharge on surface is revised monthly based on local diesel prices, which rose in mid-May after about 5–6 years. Air fuel surcharge rose from April as Brent climbed from around mid-March.
Auto is a niche express vertical; management estimates it grows at about high-teens, in line with surface B2B. Market share is hard to quantify.
Management says e-commerce pricing remains competitive, with capacity still available in the market; Blue Dart positions itself as a premium player.
Management says it gained a very small but roughly stable market share in SME clients versus last year (informal assessment).

qa_highlights.question: Is the revenue growth mainly from pricing, given volume growth was only about 7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed directionally. Pricing came from GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery (fuel surcharge offset fuel cost rises, which also lifted yield).

qa_highlights.question: Why is e-commerce growth lower than the industry, and is it a focus area?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce is a growth driver but not a mass-volume focus. It is prioritising premium, time-critical traffic that fits its capacity, and it is not targeting the largest e-commerce share.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and new hubs?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone annualised capex is INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Two major northern hubs and some medium eastern hubs were added, and southern and Mumbai hub consolidation is being considered a few quarters away.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins, and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 brings volume opportunity but also resourcing challenges. It aims to keep or improve margins through efficiency and better realisation, without quantifying either.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2 recently acquired aircraft stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said pallet utilisation was restored to pre-acquisition levels by 2024. The aircraft are part of the wider network, and capacity is not a constraint; yield is the main lever.

risks_watch: Growth quality: about 7% tonnage growth against about 15% revenue growth implies most of the increase came from pricing and surcharges, which may not persist.
Fuel: diesel and Brent rises were passed through with a lag; Q2 is expected to show the full surcharge effect, but any fall in fuel prices would reverse it.
Air volume growth of about 2.6% versus surface about 9% suggests air is stagnating in volume.
H2 resourcing: management flagged that peak-season flex will decide margins.
Competition in e-commerce pricing remains intense, with spare capacity in the market.
BFSI (documents and cards) is no longer growing, and the 25–30% documents-plus-parcels exposure needs monitoring.
Management declined to provide e-commerce split by air and surface, D2C share, or yield premium figures, limiting visibility.

526797|2026-03.overview: Greenply reported its highest-ever quarterly consolidated revenue of INR776.2 crore in Q4 FY26, with core EBITDA of INR93.2 crore at a 12% margin. MDF delivered its record quarter at INR189.4 crore revenue and 17% margin, while plywood volume grew 15.6% YoY. Management flagged a CEO/JMD resignation, a tax search operation, and a INR15.16 crore exceptional impairment linked to the Dubai entity, and guided to a 0.7-0.72 peak debt-to-equity during the MDF capex cycle. Part of Q4 volume growth was attributed to channel stocking in the second half of March, and chemical costs rose sharply, prompting price increases from April.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR588.5 crore, volume +15.6% and value +14.6% YoY, core EBITDA margin 10.4% (+120 bps YoY). FY26 revenue INR2,105.7 crore (+7.5%), volume +8.3%, margin 8.8%. Price hikes of 4-5% effective April 2026; management attributes gross margin dip to product mix.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 record revenue INR189.4 crore on 62,000 CBM (+45.3% volume YoY), margin 17%. FY26 revenue INR635.6 crore (+19.9%), margin 13.4%. Price increases of 5% and 10% effective April 2026 (15% total per analyst confirmation); FY27 volume guidance 25-30%.

segments.name: Furniture & fittings JV
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales INR12.99 crore; FY26 revenue INR44.27 crore with PAT loss INR50.8 crore (Greenply share INR25.4 crore). Management expects breakeven around the middle of next year.

guidance_outlook: Plywood volume growth target of 10% for the rest of FY27, with margins held at recent levels contingent on volume delivery.
MDF volume growth of 25-30% in FY27, using near-full capacity; EBITDA margins to be kept consistent with recent performance (Q4 FY26 MDF margin 17% described as sustainable).
Management expects the March 2026 quarter consolidated margin to be the new norm, with H2 FY27 plywood margin upside from new process technology.
Peak debt-to-equity expected at 0.7-0.72 during FY27 or the year after, reverting to 0.5-0.6 the following year.
Effective tax rate around 22% (standalone 22%, subsidiaries around 17%).

Odisha plywood plant capex about INR130 crore; other plywood technology improvements about INR45-50 crore; MDF capex about INR425 crore, of which about INR300 crore falls in FY27 and INR125 crore in FY28.
capex_capacity: PVC and WPC plant commenced commercial production in April 2026 with installed capacity of 6 million kg for doors and 3 million kg for door frames; peak revenue potential INR75-80 crore.
New MDF facility: civil construction underway and key machinery ordered; management says on track. About INR10 crore paid as advance to main equipment supplier so far.
Plywood greenfield facility (Odisha) under construction at full pace with major orders placed.

Plywood process change (ContiRoll technology): implemented in 2 of 4 existing facilities, remaining 2 to be done in FY27. Management says it lowers cost, manpower and material use and improves quality.
Flooring line in MDF expected to be fully operational in early Q2 FY27, with annual top-line capacity of about INR70-75 crore at peak.
Management says investment per cubic metre on the new Conti capacity is lower, aiming to improve capex turnover and ROCE. Steady-state ROCE aspiration of 18-20% at peak utilisation.
demand_pricing: Chemical prices rose over 50% early in the quarter; chemicals are about 30% of MDF raw material cost. Price increases: MDF 5% and 10% (15% total per analyst question confirmed by management) and plywood 4-5%, effective April 2026. Management says chemical prices have stabilised.

Q4 volume growth partly reflected channel stocking in the second half of March, plus a shift from unorganised to organised players as small MDF and plywood players were disrupted by cash-tight supplier terms.
Industry MDF growth estimated at 15-20% annualised; plywood industry growth 3-4%. Management estimates Greenply MDF market share about 7% currently, peaking at 8-8.5%.
Timber prices stable in Q4 and expected flat for FY27. Imports of MDF largely wiped out due to BIS and dollar/freight conditions.
Receivable days rose by about 3 days from December 2025 (analyst cited 47 to 54 days YoY), attributed to OEM growth and furniture factory business; management says receivables are LC-protected.
Advertising spend in Q4 lower YoY; management says the annual amount is unchanged and it is timing of expense recognition.

qa_highlights.question: Is MDF margin sustainable and is plywood double-digit margin sustainable with quality issues in the lower-end brand fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says MDF margin is sustainable, driven by volume and operating leverage on fixed costs, with cost increases already passed on. Plywood margin is sustainable if volume targets are met; process changes have improved quality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the balance sheet trajectory after capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-equity may peak at 0.7-0.72 in one year, then return to 0.5-0.6 the following year; management does not want substantially higher debt.

qa_highlights.question: Are the one-offs (Dubai/GMEL, forex) behind the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no further challenges, with all potential liability on equity, corporate guarantees and loan advances provided for in the books.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 volume growth inflated by channel inventory, and does Q1 FY27 continue the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management partly agreed, noting some stocking in the second half of March, and attributed growth mainly to a shift from unorganised to organised players; Q1 FY27 has started strongly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and split of growth capex?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR425 crore MDF capex, roughly INR300 crore in FY27 and INR125 crore in FY28; Odisha plywood about INR130 crore; plywood technology upgrades INR45-50 crore. Analyst estimated about INR480 crore for FY27, which management said was almost right.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MDF gross margin volatile and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q2 and Q3 volatility to line extension disruption and trading mix; Q4 FY26 margin is the base to deliver going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the income tax search conducted and is there any liability?
qa_highlights.answer: Search covered Greenply, Greenlam and Greenpanel; management said the reason is not known, no order or demand has been received, and the auditor has noted no liability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the JMD and CEO Manoj Tulsian step down, and is there a change in strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: He stepped down to pursue personal commitments and will continue as an advisor; sales, plant, IT, HR and marketing heads are in place, and a full-time replacement at his level is not planned immediately.

526797|2026-06.headline: Greenply Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.7% YoY to INR724.9 crore, with core EBITDA margin of 10.8%, up 50 bps YoY.
526797|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR724.9 crore (up 20.7% YoY) and core EBITDA was INR78.3 crore at a 10.8% margin. Plywood and MDF both delivered double-digit volume growth, but management said Q1 sales were lost to election-related labour disruption, lower plant utilisation (92-93% vs ~98-99% in Q4) and weak outsourcing. Price increases of 7-9% in MDF and 3-5% in plywood were taken, and the new MDF flooring line started commercial production on 20 July 2026. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 10% plywood volume growth and 25-30% MDF volume growth, and a 10% plywood margin.

segments.name: MDF

qa_highlights.question: Why did plywood EBITDA margin fall QoQ even though gross margin improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed low absolute volumes in Q1 versus Q4 (~600+ crore quarterly run-rate), plus election-related labour shortages, lower outsourcing and utilisation of 92-93%. It reiterated the 10% margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable MDF EBITDA margin, and the upside after the second line?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity supports 16-17% margin on a sustainable basis; the second line's operating leverage could add ~1% more, so 18% is possible.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the MDF gross margin decline of ~300 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Sharp timber cost rise from monsoon-season moisture and cutting disruption; management expects timber prices to stay stable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the employee cost increase and what is the normalised run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase reflects a provision for April wage increments plus lower sales. Q1 employee cost was ~INR98.88 crore; management expects ~INR100 crore per quarter for the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR500 crore total: parent ~INR47 crore (incl. SAMET loss funding), GSPL ~INR100 crore, GSPPL ~INR300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and leverage path?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt INR710-730 crore at 31 March 2027 (0.75x D/E), falling below 0.7x six months later and to ~0.65-0.7x by year-end. Term loan cost ~7-7.25%, working capital ~7%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the furniture JV revenue flat because of deliberate choice or weak demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed weak BIS enforcement, continued cheap Chinese imports and the need to cut imported product prices once made in India; it expects losses to reach zero around mid-next year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROCE targets for MDF and the path to them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 17-18% ROCE over a five-to-seven-year cycle. It said this requires selling 100% of capacity profitably and lower capex per cbm on line two.

526797|2026-09.headline: Greenply Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.1% YoY to INR799.7 crores, with core EBITDA margin up 300 bps to 11.2%; MDF volumes missed on production disruptions.
526797|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR799.7 crores (+16.1% YoY) and core EBITDA was INR89.2 crores at an 11.2% margin, up 300 bps YoY. Plywood value grew 15.5% on 6.1% volume growth, helped by premium mix and a realisation of INR264 per sq m. MDF revenue grew 18.4% in value but volume and realisation fell QoQ after price-hike rollbacks and monsoon and maintenance disruptions. Management kept plywood guidance, cut MDF full-year volume guidance to about 20% growth while holding a 15-16% margin, and announced a 15 million sq m Sandila plywood expansion at INR125 crores capex.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR625.7 crores, volume +6.1% YoY, realisation INR264 per sq m, core EBITDA margin 10.05%. Management attributes the margin gain to premium and Green product mix and says plant utilisation exceeded 100%.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR173.9 crores, volume 54,605 CBM, realisation INR31,816 per CBM (down QoQ after price-hike rollback), EBITDA margin 15.2%. Production was about 53,000 CBM against about 54,000 CBM sold, so the volume shortfall was supply-side.

segments.name: SAMET furniture fittings JV
segments.commentary: Q2 sales INR14.08 crores with a JV PAT loss of INR12.6 crores (Greenply share INR6.3 crores). Greenply says it stopped funding losses from Q1 and will dilute its stake to 19% by a January 5 end date.

segments.name: HDF flooring
segments.commentary: Commercial production started in July 2026. Management expects contribution from H2 FY27 and targets INR2-3 crores a month to begin with.

guidance_outlook: Plywood: existing guidance maintained. H2 plywood EBITDA margin expected at 10%+, provided sales cross about INR600 crores a quarter. Management expects more than 10% plywood volume growth annually.

MDF: full-year volume growth cut to about 20% (from earlier guidance), with 63,000 CBM targeted in each of Q3 and Q4. Core EBITDA margin guided at 15-16%; management says it can sustain above INR5,000 per CBM.

Sandila plywood expansion: 15 million sq m, INR125 crores capex, funded by debt and equity, commercial production in Q4 FY28; revenue potential INR320-340 crores at full utilisation. Total plywood capacity becomes 81.3 million sq m from Q4 FY28.

Odisha greenfield plywood facility expected in about two quarters; Vadodara MDF expansion expected in Q2 FY28 (the transcript says Plywood in Q4 FY27 and MDF in Q2 FY28, which conflicts with the Odisha and Sandila timing given elsewhere).
SAMET: dilution to 19% targeted by January 5 (head of terms signed). Greenply expects brand-charge income and zero further drag thereafter.
Chipboard: multi-day press line of about INR100 crores capex per line, 250-300 CBM output per line, asset turn about 1:2; first line planned next year or the year after.
capex_capacity: Sandila (Lucknow) plywood: 15 million sq m new capacity, INR125 crores capex, commercial production Q4 FY28; total plywood capacity 81.3 million sq m from Q4 FY28.
MDF Vadodara expansion: management says Q2 FY28 start; the new MDF line is running ahead of schedule per management. Current line produces about 60,000 CBM per quarter.
Odisha greenfield plant: about two quarters to start for Odisha, and about four to five quarters for Sandila, per management's Q&A remarks.
Pre-lam plywood for furniture makers: trials done, full-scale commercial production expected from November 2026.

Agroforestry carbon program: first phase covers over 2,300 hectares across Gujarat and Nagaland; second stage targets 12,000 hectares; 2,56,688 carbon credits allotted. Management says 50-60% of Vadodara timber sourcing and 100% of Nagaland sourcing now come through the program.
demand_pricing: Plywood: management says competition in pricing is very high, and the Q1 price increase of about 15.5% has been almost fully passed back. Raw-material chemical costs are up about 7-8% permanently, while other inputs are stable. Management attributes the margin hold to mix, Pre-lam and plain-board growth, energy-cost savings and operating efficiencies.

MDF: new capacity from Action TESA (south) has started, and Elixir is starting up soon. Management expects unorganised players to exit within 6-12 months and sees the next 12 months as weak. It describes imports as a limited threat because of freight and geopolitics.
Timber prices are stable, and management assumes no further increase. Any decline would be a margin windfall.
Carbon credits: a sample credit sold at USD15; management estimates INR25-30 crores of revenue at that price, with Greenply's share at 10-20%.
Management targets ROCE of about 18%+ over 3-5 years for MDF, and says the short-term return is low.

qa_highlights.question: Why did plywood growth slow to 6% this quarter after 10%+ in prior quarters? Any strategy change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no strategy shift. Plant utilisation was above 100%, so capacity was prioritised for premium products and margin, with the TermiVax campaign helping. Management does not expect this constraint after Odisha starts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MDF volume fall QoQ and what drives the volume and price trends?
qa_highlights.answer: The shortfall was production-driven: monsoon disruption and an OEM annual maintenance that ran four days against one planned. 526807|2026-03.headline: Seamec Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 58% YoY to Rs330 crore and PAT more than doubled to Rs103 crore; FY27 growth guided at about 15%.

526807|2026-06.headline: Seamec Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 41% YoY to INR 297 crore, with EBITDA of INR 124 crore (about 42% margin).

Management attributed the quarter to higher vessel deployment, healthy utilisation and cost discipline, with Paladin's dry-dock and the Middle East conflict weighing on the onshore segment. Margins: management guides 40-42% EBITDA margin, sustainable on an annualised basis; quarterly figures not guided.

Seamec ANANT: acquisition (USD 70 million, funded about 50:50 internal equity and loans) expected to complete by end-August 2026; deployment on ONGC contract about one month after acquisition for statutory formalities, with start expected within Q2 FY27 per Naveen Mohta and in Q3 per Sunil Gupta; expected 95-98% utilisation once working.
Gallant vessel sale: expected to complete in September 2026 after shareholder approval.

526829|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 117% YoY to INR2,408 crore and PAT more than tripled to about INR62.6 crore, driven mainly by LPG volumes.

Most company-specific numbers (segment revenue split, FY26 capex, LPG import volumes, Type 4 cylinder margins) were deferred to follow-up emails.

Management says Malur is now fully operational, the paint shop phase one went live in June 2026, and shipments to the largest customer have started. Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin of 8–11% and a ~20% revenue CAGR over three years. Funding of the expansion pipeline with a mix of borrowings and accruals; company says it is not generating enough cash for large projects alone.

530005|2026-03.headline: UltraTech Q4 FY26: consolidated volume about 44 Mt, EBITDA of INR1,253/t, and a INR240/share FY26 dividend, with India Cements brand migration completed.
530005|2026-03.overview: The call was the UltraTech Q4 FY26 earnings call, transcript filed by India Cements Ltd as a subsidiary disclosure. UltraTech crossed 200 Mt India capacity and committed to 242.5 Mt by FY28. Q4 realisations rose about 2.5% on grey cement pricing, with consolidated EBITDA per tonne at INR1,253 (INR1,296 excluding acquired assets). Management flagged West Asia-linked cost pressure, mainly bags (about INR90 crore hit in March) and a mark-to-market forex loss (about INR120-130 crore), and said price hikes taken in April offset it. The Board recommended a INR240/share dividend for FY26, and India Cements' 100% brand migration to UltraTech was completed at end-March 2026.

UltraTech brand volume up 19% YoY as stated
first profit after a long time, as stated
as stated by CFO in closing remarks

segments.commentary: Utilisation fell from 100% pre-conflict to about 80%, now recovering. Bulk-only, so no bag cost. Q4 EBITDA INR278 crore.

segments.commentary: Already operating at more than INR1,000/t EBITDA in Q4 per management. Brand migration fully complete.

No thermal capacity to be added; the mix shifts to WHRS and renewables. Lead distance 367 km; new Lucknow bulk terminal.
