segments.name: Retail vs institutional
segments.commentary: Retail was about 78% of FY26 revenue, with institutional the balance. Management said retail grew faster while the enterprise business did not do well in FY26.

segments.name: Vitrified vs non-vitrified
segments.commentary: Vitrified utilisation was about 80% per management's estimate; non-vitrified was not quantified but was described as higher, possibly around 90% in Q4.

segments.name: Adhesives
segments.commentary: Still in pilot-stage expansion in select North and East India geographies; epoxy, grout and spatula added in the last 2-3 months. Management expects decent volumes in FY27 but gave no figures.

segments.name: Anti-static and antimicrobial tiles
segments.commentary: Some orders received, but management said contribution remains very small and not enough to move the top line.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance on sales growth, volumes or capacity utilisation for FY27; management said it does not give forward guidance.
Management expects Q1 FY27 to see the remaining part of the gas/energy cost increase, since cost increases began around 9-10 March and part was covered in Q3 and Q4.
Management said there is no downward price movement likely in the next few months, and definitely not in Q1, as Gujarat gas June pricing is expected to rise about INR5 per cubic metre.
Management expects FY26 margins to be better than FY25, and said margins have improved year-on-year for the last three quarters.
Capex: no major capacity capex needed in FY27; maintenance capex is about INR10 crores plus or minus INR4-5 crores versus about INR6-7 crores in FY26.
Marketing spend is expected to rise from 3.6% of revenue toward about 4% in FY27, though this is not yet decided.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation was about 60-65% in Q4 FY26, and management said it is better than in Q3 and April-May is better than Q4.
No major capacity capex needed; capex limited to maintenance, about INR6-7 crores in FY26 and about INR10 crores plus or minus INR4-5 crores in FY27.
Company has three factories outside the Morbi cluster, which supply the bulk of sales and helped stock availability.

Gas allocation was cut to about 50% at one point roughly 10 weeks before the call, leading management to consider shutting some lines; the company uses biofuels in spray dryers at Sikandrabad for 7-8 years.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price increase of about 20% in March and April 2026 (about 15-16% in March, 5-6% in April); the company said it was among the first to raise prices around 10 March.
Management said all cost increases have been passed on to consumers so far, and further increases depend on gas prices.
Dealers are cautious and reducing stock to avoid high-priced inventory; a dealer working-capital squeeze and wait-and-watch behaviour in large projects were cited.

Morbi: over 500 units reopened from 1 May, mostly GVT; ceramic output is lower, with labour shortages constraining polishing and packing. Management said Morbi design-level stocks have run down after no production in late March and April.
Management said Morbi oversupply has been cut by the crisis; exports were flat in FY26 and the unorganised sector did poorly.
Digital initiatives: 50,000 new designs added monthly by dealers via AI room visualisation; online lead generation contributing sales for 350-plus dealers monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins sustain around Q4 levels given gas price pressure, and have price hikes been taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the margin trajectory to continue; Q4 margin was 7.7% versus about 6% in Q3 (per management's description). Price hikes of about 20% were taken in March-April and further gradual increases are expected depending on gas and diesel prices.

qa_highlights.question: What are gas prices and the Q4 blended INR per SCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas pricing is formula-linked and changes every few days, with the mix moving from 80% formula to 55% normal and 45% spot. Overall gas prices are up about 30%, and Q4 blended cost averaged about INR45 per SCM.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company undertake capex now that debt is repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: No capacity capex is needed in FY27 given existing capacity; capex will be for maintenance, around INR10 crores plus or minus INR4-5 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue goes to marketing?
qa_highlights.answer: Marketing was 3.6% of revenue in FY26 and is expected to creep up toward about 4%, with no final decision taken.

qa_highlights.question: Will capacity utilisation rise above 80% and will the company gain share from unorganised players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide on FY27 utilisation, citing gas uncertainty. It said it is better placed to gain share from Morbi disruption due to its balance sheet and sell-out model, and that OBTX share could rise, though it has not quantified the split.

qa_highlights.question: How are price hikes expected to play out, and is there demand slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects realisations to readjust over about 3-4 months as gas costs normalise; tile is 1-2% of project cost, so customers are not expected to defer purchases. Management said it has seen no demand slowdown, with the Q4 volume growth figure cited.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR1.28 crore exceptional item and the fall in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: The exceptional item is the one-time labour code provision for retirement benefits at 50% of salary. Other expenses fell to INR31.8 crores from INR33.6 crores in Q4, mainly from lower travel and design costs; FY26 other expenses were at a similar level to FY25.

risks_watch: Gas price volatility and allocation cuts; formula-linked pricing changes every few days, and June Gujarat gas pricing is expected to rise about INR5 per cubic metre.
Demand after price hikes of about 20%: dealer destocking, working-capital squeeze and project wait-and-watch behaviour.
Q1 FY27 margin impact from the remaining energy cost increase, as cost increases began 9-10 March.
Morbi reopening pace and labour constraints, which could change competitive pricing; some pricing may reverse as gas costs ease within about 3-4 months.
Adhesives and anti-static product contribution remains small; the adhesive business is still at pilot stage.
530365|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on profitability, the balance sheet and market share opportunity, but cautious and evasive on forward guidance, citing gas-supply uncertainty; management repeatedly declined to give FY27 volume, margin or utilisation numbers.
key_quotes: Our strong balance sheet and success in cost management enables us to manage any volatility which might be seen in the short-term.
As utilization levels continue to improve, the benefit of operating leverages are becoming increasingly visible in the business.
So as of now, we have passed on all the cost increase to the consumer.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: Q1 FY27 near term, then 3-4 months
rows.why: Q4 margin 7.7% vs ~6% in Q3 on ~20% price hikes, but Q1 FY27 still absorbs remaining gas cost rise (June Gujarat gas up ~INR5/SCM) and realisations may readjust down over 3-4 months as gas normalises.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation only ~60-65% in Q4 FY26 and management says no major capacity capex is needed in FY27, so no new capacity is expected to come live.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 volumes +7% YoY and FY26 +4.4%, but ~20% price hikes and dealer destocking, plus Morbi reopening and gas allocation cuts, make FY27 volume growth conditional; no numeric guidance given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 60-65% with ample spare capacity; capex limited to maintenance of ~INR10 crore (+/-4-5) in FY27 versus INR6-7 crore in FY26.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numerical guidance and declined to forecast volumes, margins or utilisation citing gas uncertainty; said FY26 margins beat FY25.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Remaining gas cost increase hits Q1 FY27, June gas price expected up ~INR5/SCM, and realisations may reverse in 3-4 months as gas eases; gas allocation was cut to ~50% about 10 weeks before the call.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Adhesives in pilot-stage expansion in select North and East geographies with epoxy, grout and spatula added in last 2-3 months; management expects decent FY27 volumes but gave no figures, and anti-static/antimicrobial contribution is very small.

rows.label: Price reversal as gas costs ease
rows.why: Management expects realisations to readjust over about 3-4 months as gas costs normalise, after ~20% cumulative hikes in March-April 2026 (15-16% March, 5-6% April).

rows.label: Dealer destocking and project wait-and-watch
rows.why: Dealers are cutting stock to avoid high-priced inventory and large projects are in wait-and-watch mode after the ~20% price increase, which could slow near-term sell-in.

rows.label: Marketing spend step-up
rows.why: Marketing expected to rise from 3.6% of revenue in FY26 toward about 4% in FY27, though not yet decided, which would absorb part of the margin gain.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability, debt-free balance sheet and share gains from Morbi disruption, but declined to give FY27 volume, margin or utilisation numbers citing gas uncertainty; analysts pushed on gas costs, price sustainability and demand after the ~20% hikes.

530365|2026-06.headline: Orient Bell Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42.8% YoY to INR203 crores, with EBITDA margin at 8.7% and a record 39.7% gross margin.
530365|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 42.8% YoY to INR203 crores on 22.9% volume growth and about 15.9% higher ASP, with EBITDA up to INR17.6 crores from INR5.6 crores. Management attributed the quarter to Morbi shutdowns (late March to mid-May) that opened a supply gap, plus its own demand-generation push and dealer sell-out support. The company remains debt-free, reports a working capital cycle of 18 days, and is weighing deployment of its cash. Management declined to give any revenue or margin guidance.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: South volume grew about 37% and West about 60% in Q1; retail has grown faster than enterprise in recent quarters.

segments.name: Projects
segments.commentary: Project revenue was 18% of Q1 sales, including retail-sourced projects above 3,000 meters and key account projects.

segments.name: GVT (glazed vitrified tiles)
segments.commentary: GVT was about 47% of Q1 sales by value; about 15-20% of GVT came from Dora plant, bulk from SKD, and a low single-digit share from Morbi.

segments.name: Tile adhesives (Masterbond)
segments.commentary: Early-stage, cash-and-carry business with INR2.5 crores of sales in Q1, currently scaling in North and part of East India.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give revenue or margin guidance; it cited volatile Middle East and gas-price conditions.
Current gas prices are broadly stable, with July close to Q1 levels; no price cuts taken yet, with management monitoring the market.
Management said it is watching the market and will be competitive if selling prices soften.
Company is holding INR75 crores-plus in cash and plans to announce deployment of the larger part over the next three to four months.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation rose to 73% in Q1 from 64% in Q4 and about 60% blended in FY26.
Plan to invest around INR10 crores to convert 1 million meters of existing ceramic capacity to GVT.
Small capex of about INR15 crores over the next four to five months, internally financed, covering line conversion, digital printing machine replacement and polishing machines.
Next phase of manufacturing expansion under evaluation; decision expected in two to three months.
No plans to enter bathware; focus on tiles plus adhesives.
demand_pricing: Price increase of about 18-19% taken versus pre-war levels, with almost all of it realised.
Sell-out was about 40% of primary sales in Q1 versus 26% last year; DSO improved by 5 days.
Morbi-Organised gap narrowed to INR50-55 from about INR100 on comparable products, which benefits organised players.
Dealers are adding suppliers in other geographies to reduce dependence on Morbi.

Gas: Q1 average about INR60 per unit; Sikandrabad (North) moved from INR44-45 pre-war to INR60-62. Morbi exports fell to about INR800 crores a month average in April-May versus INR1,500-1,600 crores earlier.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase was taken in Q1 and are prices sustainable as gas prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increase of about 18-19% versus pre-war, almost fully realised; no cuts yet, with management watching gas and Morbi pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 23% volume growth and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Morbi supply gap during the shutdown plus OBL's demand generation, with about 40% sell-out support to dealers and 24/7 TV advertising; management pointed to input KPIs rather than guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Dora plant utilisation, and share of GVT and EBITDA from it?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant-level utilisation is misleading due to inter-plant transfers; South and West growth was used as proxy. About 15-20% of GVT comes from Dora.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 revenue and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Company policy is no guidance on revenue or margins; management cited positive quarter-on-quarter KPIs only.

qa_highlights.question: Use of about INR75 crores of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR15 crores of internally financed capex over four to five months; the larger part is to be invested in the business, with a decision in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Tile adhesives progress and bathware plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhesives generated INR2.5 crores in Q1 on a cash-and-carry basis, expanding from North to East; no bathware plans.

risks_watch: Gas and propane prices remain volatile; any fall could force price cuts, and management has not yet committed to holding prices.
Morbi capacity is back at full run-rate since mid-May, so the supply-gap tailwind may fade.
Exports from Morbi remain depressed by higher freight costs (5-6x to Gulf).
Deployment of about INR75 crores of cash and the next manufacturing expansion are undecided.
530365|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on results and market share, but cautious and non-committal on outlook, repeatedly declining guidance and calling pricing and gas costs too volatile to forecast.
key_quotes: Our demand generation initiatives have ensured a sellout of approximately 40% of the primary sales volume in Q1 versus 26% sellout last year.
As a result, we achieved our highest ever gross margin of 39.7% during this quarter.
As a policy, we do not give any guidance for future.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR0.6 crores YoY

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin hit 8.7% (+480 bps YoY) and gross margin a record 39.7%, but a 18-19% price increase is at risk if gas (Q1 avg ~INR60/unit, up from INR44-45 at Sikandrabad) falls and Morbi supply gap closes as Morbi is back at full run-rate since mid-May.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation at 73% (up from 64% in Q4, ~60% blended FY26); ~INR10 crores GVT conversion of 1 million meters and INR15 crores line/printing/polishing capex over 4-5 months add modest capacity, while the next manufacturing phase decision is due in 2-3 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 volume grew 22.9% on a Morbi supply gap, sell-out now ~40% of primary (vs 26%), and South/West retail up ~37%/~60%, but Morbi back at full run-rate since mid-May means the tailwind may fade.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: next 2-3 months for the next manufacturing phase; deployment
rows.why: Utilisation at 73% and rising, with the next expansion phase under evaluation with a decision in 2-3 months and INR75 crores-plus cash to be deployed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management explicitly declines revenue or margin guidance as a policy and cites volatile Middle East and gas-price conditions.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: No price cuts yet, but management says it will be competitive if selling prices soften, and gas-price moves and fading Morbi supply gap could compress ASP (up ~15.9% YoY) and volume growth (22.9%).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Tile adhesives (Masterbond) at INR2.5 crores Q1 sales is scaling from North to East India; GVT conversion of 1 million meters is approved, though no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: Price cuts if gas and Morbi pricing soften
rows.why: About 18-19% price increase taken vs pre-war, almost fully realised, with no cuts yet; management says it will be competitive if selling prices soften.

rows.label: Deployment of INR75 crores-plus cash
rows.why: Company is debt-free with INR75 crores-plus in cash and plans to announce deployment of the larger part over the next three to four months.

rows.label: Dealer sell-out and supplier diversification
rows.why: Sell-out at ~40% of primary sales vs 26% last year and DSO improved by 5 days, while dealers add suppliers in other geographies to reduce Morbi dependence.

tone.note: Management was confident on results, market share and the 18-19% price increase, but cautious and non-committal on outlook, repeatedly declining guidance over volatile gas prices and Middle East conditions; analysts probed on sustainability of volume and pricing, Dora utilisation and use of cash.

530365|2026-09.headline: Orient Bell H1 FY27 revenue grew 18.1% with Q2 EBITDA margin of 9.8%, driven by ~18% volume growth and ~18-20% price increases.
530365|2026-09.overview: Orient Bell reported strong Q2 and H1 FY27 results, with Q2 revenue growth of 14.6% and H1 growth of 18.1%, which management described as industry-leading. Management attributed growth to a secondary-sales focus, digital tools for dealers, and price increases taken from July, while cutting credit in the market. Profitability improved sharply, with Q2 PBT of Rs 16.4 crore (up 326%) and EBITDA margin of about 9.8%, and the working capital cycle fell to 18 days from 20 days in March 2026. Capacity utilisation reached 75% in Q2 after conversion of 1.2 million sq m of ceramic capacity to GVT in October 2026.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 740 crore (as stated in transcript, 'stood at 40 crores' unclear)

segments.name: GVT (glazed vitrified tiles)
segments.commentary: GVT share of sales rose to about 45% currently from roughly 20% in FY22-23, after conversion of 1.2 million sq m ceramic capacity to GVT completed in October 2026.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: North and Central ~49% of sales, East ~24%; management plans to expand presence in South via TV advertising in Tamil and Kannada and new shop-in-shop displays.

segments.name: Retail vs project mix
segments.commentary: Retail vs project split held at about 80:20; projects defined as sales above 3,000 sq m per quarter.

segments.name: Master Bond (adhesives) and new products
segments.commentary: Anti-static, foldable tiles and tile adhesive (Master Bond) are early-stage, differentiation-focused; Master Bond dispatched from four locations, with expected sales of Rs 3-5 crore per quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give formal Q3/Q4 guidance but said double-digit EBITDA margin is expected in H2, with H2 historically stronger than H1.
Gas prices: November 2026 expected to stay at about Rs 83 per unit; December uncertain.
FY27 capex about Rs 20 crore including maintenance; next-year capex plan to be decided in the coming months.
Plans to open new exclusive showrooms starting H2 FY27; about 238-240 touchpoints currently active, with about 200 more shop-in-shop formats planned.
capex_capacity: Conversion of 1.2 million sq m ceramic capacity into GVT completed in October 2026; capacity utilisation 75% in Q2.
Invested about Rs 1.1 crore for 1 MW renewable energy capacity at Dora facility, now powering utilities with green energy.
Management said further ceramic-to-GVT conversion is unlikely; future capacity additions will be new lines.
Own manufacturing gross margin about 38-39%, with Dora expected to be similar within about 1%.
demand_pricing: Volume growth about 15-18% in H1 versus industry volume growth of about 1% excluding OBL; management says market share improved (listed-player share small, industry dominated by unorganised).
Average selling price up about Rs 12 per sq m QoQ (Q2 about Rs 333 vs Q1 about Rs 321); price increases of roughly 18-20% in aggregate, with the last hike in July 2026.
Industry volatility from gas prices; management said 40-50% of manufacturers were shut and may stay closed through November, which could limit further price cuts.
Credit in the market reduced while growing; large low-margin projects declined in favour of mid and small projects.

qa_highlights.question: Geographical split of revenue and plans for the South?
qa_highlights.answer: North and Central 49%, East 24%. Management is building South presence via TV ads in Tamil and Kannada and dealer shop-in-shop displays, with exclusive showrooms to follow in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Current price hike status and whether prices are sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Last hike in July; Q2 average selling price up about Rs 12 QoQ to about Rs 333. Management said further price cuts are unlikely given closures among competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs price contribution to growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% volume and about 20% price contribution cited for the quarter, per management's breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: What is needed to reach double-digit EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 margin was 9.8%; management expects double-digit margin in H2 by staying on execution priorities and said gas price declines would be passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Progress of new products (anti-static, foldable tiles, Master Bond adhesive)?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet significant contributors; mainly differentiation tools. Master Bond expected to contribute Rs 3-5 crore per quarter, leveraging dealer network.

qa_highlights.question: Capex strategy and further GVT conversions?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 20 crore capex for FY27 including maintenance; no further ceramic-to-GVT conversions planned; future capex plan to be finalised in next few months.

risks_watch: Gas price volatility and its pass-through to pricing; November at about Rs 83 and December uncertain.
Sustainability of 18-20% price increases if industry supply returns post-Diwali.
Dealer churn in exclusive showrooms, which management says it is working to arrest before expanding.
Limited South India dealer penetration versus competitors, which management did not address in detail.
Pace of Master Bond and new product adoption, still early stage.
530365|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin trajectory, with management stating Q2 EBITDA of 9.8% and H2 double-digit margin expectation. Cautious and non-committal on forward guidance, on gas price outlook and on dealer-specific questions, which were declined.
key_quotes: The reason that we have got these good results is because as I said in my opening statement, we have successfully driven the strategy of secondary sale focus.
So we are almost there. I think quarter two was 9.8 percent this thing.
We went slow on making new boutiques, new showrooms till we fixed the reasons because of which churn was high.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin was 9.8% and management expects double-digit EBITDA margin in H2 FY27, backed by ~18-20% price hikes (last in July 2026) and gas-price pass-through.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The 1.2 million sq m ceramic-to-GVT conversion is already done (Oct 2026) and management said no further conversions are planned; utilisation of 75% leaves headroom, and only new lines would add capacity later with no date given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 volume grew about 15-18% against industry volume growth of about 1% excluding OBL, and share gains are being pursued via dealer digital tools and shop-in-shop displays.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 75% (below the 80% threshold) and FY27 capex is about Rs 20 crore including maintenance; the next-year capex plan is pending and to be decided in the coming months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined formal Q3/Q4 guidance, but H1 revenue grew 18.1% and H2 is historically stronger than H1, so there is room to beat if pricing holds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Price increases of ~18-20% could reverse if industry supply returns after Diwali, and gas prices are uncertain beyond November at about Rs 83 per unit.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Master Bond adhesive is already dispatched from four locations with expected sales of Rs 3-5 crore per quarter; anti-static and foldable tiles are early-stage and not yet significant.

rows.label: South India push via TV ads and shop-in-shop
rows.why: Management is building South presence with TV ads in Tamil and Kannada, ~200 planned shop-in-shop formats and exclusive showrooms from H2, though North and Central still make up 49% of sales and South dealer penetration is limited.

rows.label: Price sustainability of 18-20% hikes
rows.why: Average selling price rose about Rs 12 per sq m QoQ to about Rs 333, and management says competitor closures (40-50% of manufacturers shut through November) make further price cuts unlikely, but the hikes depend on supply staying tight.

rows.label: Working capital cycle at 18 days
rows.why: The cycle fell to 18 days from 20 days in March 2026 as credit to the market was cut, and this could hold or improve further, though the brief gives no target.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth (H1 revenue +18.1%), margin trajectory (Q2 EBITDA 9.8%, double-digit in H2) and share gains, but declined formal Q3/Q4 guidance, gas-price outlook and dealer-specific questions; the brief does not show detailed analyst pushback.

530367|2026-03.headline: NRB Bearings Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to INR372 crores, EBITDA margin 19.5%, and FY26 PAT up 77% to INR146 crores.
530367|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to INR372 crores, with EBITDA up 17% to INR74 crores (19.5% margin) and PAT of INR42 crores. For FY26, revenue rose 11% to INR1,335 crores, EBITDA rose 19% to INR267 crores, and margin expanded to 19.5% from 18.3%. Management attributed margin gains to solar power, automation, yield improvement and renegotiated vendor costs, and flagged a quarter-end forex anomaly that pulled down Q4 gross margin. Management leaned on an FY-level lens, declined to disclose standalone export, aftermarket, and segment splits, and guided to brownfield capacity commissioning from June-July 2026.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Management says NRB is in transmission, driveline, chassis and steering, with limited engine exposure beyond two- and three-wheelers and little wheel-end content. Replacement market grew about 4%, and the company said it shifted focus toward OEMs in Q4.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Industrial business is about 14-15% of revenue per management, including tractors and farm equipment. Target is 20-25% of revenue over time; named focus areas are construction equipment, off-highway, gearboxes, switchgear, power generation and electric grid.

segments.name: Aerospace (Mahant Toolroom, acquired subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mahant Toolroom order book is close to INR50 crores, up from INR25 crores at announcement, with all orders from HAL across divisions. Management expects full operational control between mid-April and May 2026 and a business plan in about six months.

guidance_outlook: International business expected to grow 10-14% in FY27 per current business plan, with management saying maybe up to 15%.

FY27 capex guided at about INR120 crores (including land), against a total announced INR200 crore capex over 18 months plus up to INR40 crores for land; split is 90% machines and 10% infrastructure and building.
Brownfield capacity enhancements to commission from June-July 2026 through FY27 and up to Q1 2028, with partial benefits from the current quarter.
Management aims to sustain EBITDA margins of 18-21% over time; industrial products expected to be as profitable as the core, with individual products ranging from 14% to 30%.
Five-year aspirational revenue target of about INR2,500 crores, which management said is increasingly becoming a concrete goal.
Mahant Toolroom business plan to be shared in about six months; AS9100-linked aerospace certification expected in about six months.
capex_capacity: Reported capacity utilisation about 85%; management says effective utilisation at several plants is much closer to full after adjusting for demand variation, maintenance, shifts and changeovers.
Bottlenecks identified at specific plants; machinery orders placed and first machines arrived, with major enhancement commissioning from June-July 2026.
Capex split: about 90% machines and 10% infrastructure/building/plant; maintenance, quality, new product and small balancing capex is part of normal capex at about 10% of turnover.
Joint venture declaration allows up to 20% of JV capacity to be used for automotive; about 20-25% of current automotive capacity is being used for industrial products.
Mahant Toolroom acquisition gives people, design and certification capability; the company had INR100 crores of aerospace RFQs but lacked an AS9100 plan.
demand_pricing: Management says growth came from volume, market share gains, capacity utilisation, product mix and efficiency, not one-offs.
Export demand was affected by geopolitics and logistics; India faced gas shortages, and customers changed product mix during Q4, which reduced the quarter's original plan.
Management says it prices to maintain margin profile; EV-specific bearings priced to keep existing margins and bearing content per vehicle is largely value neutral.
Company does not give export, aftermarket or standalone splits; it says the replacement market grew about 4% and that it deprioritised replacement given discount structures.
New wins include Siemens (details withheld under confidentiality), and aerospace platforms for HAL and NAL.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4% international growth standalone exports, and what are export and aftermarket growth for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reports consolidated international business (all overseas-supplied customers, including subsidiaries) at about 4% growth and declined to give standalone export or aftermarket figures; replacement market grew about 4%.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex, and what is the split between standalone and subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex for FY27 is closer to INR120 crores, including land; management declined to split standalone versus subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin dip, the first sub-60% quarter in a long time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it primarily to forex, combining product mix with high-import-content products and quarter-end rupee conversion of COGS; it said this is an accounting anomaly that should normalise.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Mahant's INR50 crore order book will convert in FY27, and is HAL 100% of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY27 revenue and said the order book pace depends on rollout rates; HAL is the sole customer but across multiple divisions.

qa_highlights.question: Will industrial be margin accretive, and when will industrial reach 20% of revenue?

Oman normalisation expected within Q1 FY27; South Africa breakeven from Q2 FY27; Saudi tire recycling plant (24,000 tpa) capex of INR20-25 crores, with work starting end Q2 or Q3 FY27.
Working capital days expected to stay at current levels, since PCMB carries higher credit terms.
capex_capacity: Tire-crush capacity in India expanded 9% to 185,000 tons in FY26; target of 235,000 tpa by FY27. Tire-crush volume rose 13% to 155,000 tons in FY26.
Capacity utilisation was 90% in India and 85% in Oman in FY26. Varale plant at 80% utilisation.
Solar capacity rose from 1.23 MW to 4.48 MW in FY26; about 50% of power needs expected from renewables from FY27.
Pyrolysis plant (100 TPD feed) and rCB plant: about INR40 crores capex, largely complete. TPO stabilisation expected by end Q1 FY27 and rCB trial production in Q2 FY27.
TP Buildtech Kolkata plant commissioned, running under 25% utilisation, with three new construction system product lines launched.
Micronized rubber powder capacity being increased at at least two plants. PCMB capacity moving from a 6,000 tpa pilot to an 18,000 tpa polymer compounding facility in Haryana.
demand_pricing: Raw material economics: virgin rubber about INR240-260/kg vs recycled rubber about INR50/kg, roughly one-fifth the cost.

Bitumen prices have almost doubled, driving stronger crumb-rubber-modified bitumen (CRMB) demand, though India's bitumen supply constraint (imports of 3-3.5 million tons) hit road-work volumes in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Realisations on reclaim rubber and MRP improved on demand; management said realisation volatility currently favours the company.
Freight rates and elevated polymer prices from the Middle East crisis raised import costs; management says the company offset these by sourcing from multiple geographies and feedstock types.
Competition from new CRMB and rCB entrants: management cites a moat from raw material, product, customer and geographic diversity, plus 2-5 year approval cycles with tire majors.

qa_highlights.question: Vision FY29 revenue breakup by segment, and EPR outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PCMB rises toward 8-10% of revenue from about 4%. Infra is expected to be about 30%, Industrial about 35%, Consumer about 10%, with the balance from rCB and pyrolysis. EPR revenue stays around INR29-30 crores a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the infra slowdown hit blended margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects better realisations on reclaim rubber and MRP to offset any infra softness, and says the bitumen-driven slowdown is temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA expected from RCB and pyrolysis plants in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined FY27 revenue of about INR50-55 crores. EBITDA margins of 15-19% are expected once the plants are fully running, with payback in line with the existing business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise from 42 to 55?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase is mainly due to PCMB, where industry practice carries longer credit days. Core rubber-products credit days have not changed materially, and working capital days are expected to stay at current levels.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR100 crore capex be funded, and what is the debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of it from internal accruals, with FY27 EBITDA projected above INR100 crores. Management may take up to about INR20 crores of debt if needed.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling bitumen supply and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The company holds no bitumen and does not trade it. It supplies modifier to IOC and to contractors who source their own bitumen, which the company says is assured business for the next couple of years.

risks_watch: Bitumen availability (India imports 3-3.5 million tons, with Iran a key supplier) may keep infra volumes soft in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Middle East tensions delay the Saudi plant capital works (now expected end Q2 or Q3 FY27) and disrupt Oman exports; Oman normalisation is expected within Q1 FY27.
Start-up losses at South Africa and new plants; South Africa breakeven targeted from Q2 FY27, and TP Buildtech margins remain under pressure from crude, polymer and currency movements.
Receivable days rose to about 55 from 42 due to PCMB credit terms; watch whether working capital intensity persists.
Competition from new CRMB and rCB entrants; management cites strong moats but no quantified pricing impact.
Consolidated PAT growth (9%) lagged EBITDA growth; FY26 revenue growth was only 8% and infra revenue fell, so FY27 20-25% growth needs execution.
key_quotes: FY26 was another year of strong execution for Tinna Rubber, despite geopolitical uncertainties and a dynamic operating environment, we achieved record tire processing volumes and delivered robust EBITDA margins of over 17%.
But we expect that to normalize immediately because India has a very aggressive program for road construction.
Our comfort level to give a guidance to market is at 18%.

I don't see us doing any inorganic acquisition related to our business, but some adjacency business, if it comes across, where we have something new to learn or a new product line to add or new geography to add, those are the ideas we remain open to and we will look at those opportunities.

530475|2026-06.headline: Tinna Rubber Q1 FY27 posted record EBITDA above INR50 crores (21%+ margin) and PAT above INR20 crores, with EPR credits adding a one-off monetisation lift.
530475|2026-06.overview: Management reported record Q1 FY27 profitability, with standalone and consolidated EBITDA margins above 21% and PAT margins above 13%. Standalone revenue rose 18% YoY and consolidated revenue rose 20%, with EBITDA margin up 638 bps standalone and 575 bps consolidated. Management attributed the margin gain mainly to gross margin expansion from cheaper feedstock and a higher mix of value-added products such as MRP and reclaimed rubber. Growth engines (PCMB, TPO/rCB, Oman, South Africa) are still ramping, and management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR670-700 crores and a sustainable 18-20% EBITDA margin.

demand_pricing: Industrial demand supported by rising raw material costs and ESG-driven tyre-maker demand; MRP and reclaimed rubber volumes growing fast.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin rise is due to inventory gains, and is there margin normalisation ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gains were very marginal. Management said the changes are systemic (raw material optionality, value-added mix), and expects some front-ended costs from new projects, so 18-20% is the sustainable range.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the 400-500 bps margin expansion; material plus inventory cost fell to 46% of sales.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main contribution came at gross margin, from cheaper raw material and higher realisation from value-added products, plus scale efficiencies. Overall EBITDA margin expanded about 4 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: How is EPR monetisation accounted for, and what is its contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said accrued EPR credits from prior years were monetised against unbilled revenue. Q1 P&L impact was already booked in FY26. Annual EPR contribution is about INR25-30 crores at PBT level. Analysts' questions on clean PAT were not fully resolved on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter Chile and Saudi Arabia, and will overseas investment scale up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Oman's limited scope and similar operating parameters for Saudi Arabia, and end-of-life tyre sourcing and hedging for South Africa and Chile. India remains the core investment focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for infrastructure given the West Asia situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bitumen shortages hit some projects, but rubberized asphalt demand rose as contractors sought cheaper alternatives. Infrastructure revenue grew 7% in Q1, and Q1 is the peak road-work season.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue guidance of INR670-700 crores was reiterated; margin should sustain at 18-20% even though Q1 was 22%.

Geopolitical risk (West Asia conflict) affecting bitumen and binder supply, Oman utilisation (78%), and the Saudi project timeline.

Q2 FY27 monsoon-related seasonality in infrastructure; capacity ramp-ups of TPO, rCB and PCMB must deliver to hit INR670-700 crores.

530475|2026-09.headline: Tinna Rubber Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31% to INR157 crores and PAT 45% to INR17 crores; H1 PAT up 60% to INR38 crores.
530475|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue reached INR157 crores (up from INR120 crores), with EBITDA of INR29 crores (18.8% margin) and PAT of INR17 crores (10.9% margin). H1 revenue rose 25% to INR313 crores, EBITDA 50% to INR63 crores (20.4% margin) and PAT 60% to INR38 crores (12.2% margin). Management said profitability moderated from Q1 due to start-up costs, geopolitical uncertainty and subsidiary performance, and reiterated FY27 guidance of about INR700 crores revenue, INR126 crores EBITDA and INR70 crores PAT. Expansion moved forward with a 40-acre Andhra Pradesh site (INR250 crores over 3 years), while the Saudi Arabia tyre recycling plant has been delayed by the West Asia conflict.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited diversity of geography, raw material base and customer base, pan-India presence, and multiple tyre origins, without commenting on competitors.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR250 crores Andhra Pradesh capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding options are open over the next 6 to 12 months given a strong balance sheet; the INR250 crores is exclusively Tinna Rubber and spread over 3 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Saudi land is allotted and contractors identified, but no advances released pending local stabilisation; Panipat is a fully depreciated plant of under 2 acres that could be moved within 3-4 months, and management is making representations to the state government.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential from Andhra Pradesh and what is Vision 2029 INR1,000 crores implication?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex to sales of 2.5-3x implies INR250-300 crores revenue from INR100 crores capex; INR1,000 crores by FY29 is reachable with Andhra and Saudi, with 5-10% variance possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other expenses rise this quarter?

530521|2026-06.headline: Virat plans Rs 95 crore primary investment in Brahm Lifestyle for 70.2% stake, pivoting toward lifestyle brands; socks contract sales ~6 million pairs.

530549|2026-06.headline: Shilpa Medicare Q1 FY27 revenue rose 43% YoY to INR469 crore with EBITDA margin of 30% and reported PAT of INR101 crore, helped by a negative tax rate.
530549|2026-06.overview: Management reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA for the fourth successive quarter, with revenue of INR469 crore (up 43% YoY), gross margin of 71%, and EBITDA of INR139 crore (30% margin). Reported PAT of INR101 crore (up 115%) was flattered by a negative tax rate from reversal of deferred tax liability as the company moves to the new tax regime; the tax rate is guided to normalise to about 25%. Credit rating was upgraded from A+ to AA-, and ROCE improved to 12.5% from 8.8% in FY25. Management declined to give numerical guidance, repeatedly pointing to pipeline launches in FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax strategy and impact of moving to the new regime?
qa_highlights.answer: Company is switching to the new regime, losing MAT credit (about 25% of tax used) and some R&D-related timing benefits; normal rate expected at about 25%, with the new regime lowering the effective rate by about 9.75 points, partly offset by MAT utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for licensing income and its margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Licensing income is well above the R&D spend behind it, but failed programs are expensed; management said licensing is not recurring like CDMO and depends on continued portfolio development.

530549|2026-09.headline: Shilpa Medicare posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of INR538 crores (+35% YoY) and EBITDA of INR151 crores at a 28% margin.
530549|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record quarterly revenue (INR538 crores, +35% YoY) and record EBITDA (INR151 crores, +37% YoY), with H1 revenue crossing INR1,000 crores for the first time. Growth was broad-based across API, formulation and biologics. Gross margin compressed by roughly 700 bps YoY and sequentially, as raw material cost to sales rose from 28.65% to 35.72%, which management attributed to higher API sales and global API raw material inflation. Net debt was steady at INR612 crores despite INR252 crores of H1 capex funded from internal accruals. Management gave no revenue or utilisation guidance on peptides, albumin or Rotigotine beyond timing milestones.

segments.name: Non-captive API
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR255 crores (+24% YoY); H1 INR470 crores (+20% YoY), driven by uptake from expanded capacity and steady specialty CDMO. Management said API delivered its highest-ever quarterly revenue, and it stopped splitting oncology and non-oncology revenue.

segments.name: Formulation
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR210 crores (+50%+ YoY); H1 INR407 crores (+70% YoY). Excluding licensing income, the base business grew 87% in the quarter, led by EU complex finished dosage formulations. India business grew 2.5x in H1, led by Nor-UDCA.

segments.name: Biologics
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR65 crores (+150% YoY); H1 INR117 crores (+92% YoY), driven by licensing and partnership deals and CDMO. Management says biologics is 12% of revenue and only Adalimumab is commercially supplied in the market.

segments.name: CDMO (newly carved out as Shilpa CDMO platform)
segments.commentary: 25-plus NCE CDMO programs; 4 late-stage programs under registration and 2 in Phase III. Management expects at least one commercialisation next year and three the year after. No CDMO revenue split was disclosed.

Enzalutamide, Abraxane and Rotigotine patch launches on track for FY28; Rotigotine now expected in H1 FY28 after a two-quarter delay from a European raw-material variation approval.
Ondansetron India launch expected in H1 FY28, pending state approvals and licences after central approval.
Nivolumab biosimilar to be filed in Europe next year (FY28); Aflibercept to be in the Indian market in FY27.
Recombinant albumin Phase III protocol approved by CDSCO and EMA; IMPD submission in Europe targeted for H2 FY27.
Peptide volume and utilisation commentary deferred to H2 of next year; albumin and excipient revenue visibility deferred to around FY28.
capex_capacity: INR252 crores capex spent in H1 FY27, funded by internal accruals.

Peptides: 4 manufacturing lines in operation, 2 more being added, with space kept for further expansion. One of the largest integrated peptide capacities in India to be commissioned by end FY27; the USD 50 million peptide investment is phased and depends on utilisation.
Peptide capacity is aimed at a mix of CDMO, GLP-1 and HPAPI; management did not disclose kilolitres or gross block.
Biologics plant at Dharwad is ready and approved, and the fermentation unit is audit-ready.
Jadcherla (US FDA) is under remediation; EU authorities re-inspected and cleared the plant. US critical filings have been moved to CMO sites.
demand_pricing: Gross margin fell about 700 bps YoY and QoQ. Management attributed this to the mix shift toward lower-margin API sales and higher global API raw material costs, and said it would persist until raw material prices settle.

Nilotinib faces new generic entrants in Europe, but management sees no big change in numbers because the product is tender-based with 1–3 year tenders. Axitinib already had multiple generic players at launch.
Nor-UDCA (NAFLD) has had zero recalls in its first year since launch.
Three complex 505(b)(2) products are commercialised, with 5-plus more in advanced development for launch over the next 2–3 years.
Biosimilar pipeline: 7 active molecules with average global sales above USD10 billion; 2 biosimilars entering human studies for EU/RoW in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall about 700 bps, and how much cost increase has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Bhutada said the strong API quarter (lower-margin) versus higher-margin formulation drove the decline. Basant Bansal's follow-up got a confirmation that raw material cost to sales rose from 28.65% to 35.72% due to higher API sales and global API raw material inflation, which will persist until prices settle.

qa_highlights.question: What peptide capacity is planned, and what utilisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is built for tonnage-scale annual volumes, and utilisation depends on customer uptake. It will comment in H2 of next year, and there is visibility on some programs that require volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Which biosimilar is closest to approval, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Nivolumab is the closest. It is planned for filing in Europe next year. Aflibercept will be in India in FY27, and Adalimumab is already marketed in India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CDMO outlook for FY28 and the late-stage programs?
qa_highlights.answer: Four late-stage programs are under registration and two are in Phase III. At least one is expected to commercialise next year and three the year after. In three of them, Shilpa supplies the API.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the CDMO platform carved out from API?
qa_highlights.answer: As a one-stop integrated partner (KSM to final API for peptides; clone development to fill-finish for biologics; in-house payload, linker, antibody and conjugation for ADC), it aims to win more programs each year. Management confirmed the carve-out was to serve CDMO clients better.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Jadcherla with the US FDA and the plant risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working with the US FDA on remediation, with no impact on revenues or the 2–3 year plan. The EU re-inspected and cleared the plant, and most US critical filings are moved to CMO sites.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Rotigotine delayed, and when will it launch?
qa_highlights.answer: A European variation approval for one raw material took an extra two quarters. The launch is now set for H1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of biologics revenue is licensing versus CDMO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said each quarter will carry a mix of CDMO, biosimilar and licensing revenue, and did not break it out.

qa_highlights.question: What share of service and licensing income is licensing, and is its gross margin 100%?
qa_highlights.answer: Alpesh Dalal declined to give the licensing split or assume 100% margin. He said there are no COGS, but related R&D and other expenses sit in those lines.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from API raw material inflation and API mix; watch whether it eases once raw material prices settle.

530555|2026-03.headline: Paramount Communications Q4 FY26 revenue rose 24.5% QoQ to INR 573 crore, but FY26 EBITDA fell to INR 117.5 crore (6% margin) on US tariff disruption.
530555|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sequential recovery: revenue INR 573 crore (+13.6% YoY, +24.5% QoQ), EBITDA incl. other income INR 38.8 crore at 6.7% margin, and PAT INR 20.5 crore. FY26 revenue rose about 23% to INR 1,912 crore, but absolute EBITDA and PAT declined YoY due to US tariffs escalating from 10% to 50% during 2025. Management redirected volumes to domestic demand, which grew about 27%, and retained a US presence at sub-economic margins. The Narmadapuram greenfield plant (INR 300 crore, Phase 1) is the main growth lever, with a stated INR 5,000 crore revenue ambition by FY31.

segments.name: Domestic B2B industrial
segments.commentary: Grew 37.3% to INR 1,001 crore in FY26, led by power cables; domestic order book at INR 508 crore (87% of order book).

segments.name: Domestic B2C and distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 10.6% to INR 179 crore in FY26.

segments.name: Domestic B2G (government/PSU)
segments.commentary: Stable at about INR 182 crore in FY26, so its share of revenue fell.

segments.name: Exports (USA-led)
segments.commentary: Grew 13.9% to INR 550 crore in FY26 despite tariffs; eight active US distributors versus two in FY22.

guidance_outlook: FY27 (informal, assuming current metal prices hold): top-line growth of 15-20% and at least 10% volume growth; no formal guidance given.
Margins expected to return to FY25 levels as a first milestone, with pre-tariff margin levels targeted by end of FY27.

Narmadapuram Phase 1: investment about INR 300 crore by FY28; partial operations from Q1 FY28; sales target about INR 500 crore in FY28 and INR 1,200 crore in FY29; expected 9-10% margin and 3-4 year payback.

Long-term aspiration: INR 5,000 crore revenue by FY31, implying doubling every 3-4 years; Phase 1 capacity alone seen at INR 3,600-4,000 crore, with Phase 2 (INR 200-300 crore capex) to exceed INR 5,000 crore.
Working capital expected to normalise within Q1 FY27 after receivables rose on Q4 back-ended dispatches.
capex_capacity: Two existing plants at Dharuhera (Haryana) and Kushkhera (Rajasthan) described as running at optimal utilisation for three to four years; physical space constraint reached.
Existing-plant capex of about INR 50-55 crore a year, over INR 160 crore across the past three years.

Narmadapuram (Madhya Pradesh): about 31 acres allotted by MPIDC and possession taken; civil works underway; long-lead machinery ordered; building construction to start shortly; commissioning from FY28.

Narmadapuram products: EHV cables up to 132 kV (starting with 33 kV, then 66 kV and 132 kV), transmission conductors, elastomeric EBeam and EPR cables, lead-sheathed rubber cables; EHV approvals expected by FY28.

Funding: about INR 122 crore of equity raised (about INR 92 crore from investors, about INR 30 crore from promoters), plus internal accruals and modest debt; current debt only about INR 110 crore of working capital limits.
demand_pricing: Management cites six demand drivers: India T&D capex of INR 3.35 lakh crore (FY26-30), renewables (210-220 GW solar and 50-60 GW wind by FY30), data centres (about 70% higher cable density for AI facilities), US grid capex above USD 1 trillion, construction capex of INR 18-19 lakh crore, and railways (FY27 budget INR 3 lakh crore).

US tariffs: 10% reciprocal tariff from 2 Apr 2025, raised to 25% in August and 50% by end-August 2025; IEEPA tariffs invalidated by US Supreme Court (Feb-Apr 2026), which management says restored India's competitiveness.
Management says it kept US presence at sub-economic margins at lower volumes; competitors from Vietnam, South Korea, Cambodia, Ecuador and Egypt had a tariff advantage in FY26.
Pricing policy: no firm-price orders with delivery beyond 3-4 months; metal is bought the next working day after order receipt; price-variation formulas increasingly accepted by customers.
Management expects Q2 FY27 onwards to see stronger US demand pull, with one or two new products to be launched in the US next quarter.
Middle East, Europe, Australia and Africa flagged as opportunistic markets, with the Middle East a focus area in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new plant reach optimum utilisation, and what is the payback and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 (INR 300 crore) targets INR 1,200 crore revenue by FY29; payback 3-4 years; margin 9-10%. No formal guidance, but 15-20% top-line growth and at least 10% volume growth assumed if metal prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the domestic market not scaled up the top line or bottom line over the past year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the constraint is capacity, not demand; the plants have run at full utilisation for four years, and the company diverted US volume to domestic. FY24 precedent: US sales fell from INR 400 crore to INR 280 crore while domestic doubled from INR 400 crore to INR 800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables roughly double, and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 65% of Q4 sales were dispatched in the second half of the quarter; over three-quarters had been realised by 15 May 2026. Working capital cycle moved only from 99 to 101 days; CFO said most dispatches are against LCs.

qa_highlights.question: Can Paramount return to FY25 margins, and what drives margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 EBITDA margin is the first milestone. Drivers: new products, US tariff normalisation, power, renewable and data-centre demand, and operating leverage on volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will EHV lead times exceed 5-6 months, and how is raw material risk handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids long-delivery firm-price orders and prefers 3-4 month horizons or price-variation clauses; EHV would follow the same policy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the longer-term aspirational revenue and margin view?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 5,000 crore by FY31; Phase 1 capacity can reach about INR 3,600-4,000 crore, and Phase 2 to exceed INR 5,000 crore. Margins expected to move towards peer range as scale grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when the balance sheet has low leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity was about INR 122 crore of the INR 300 crore project; management said it diversifies the funding mix, with working capital needs still to be bank-funded and current debt about INR 110 crore.

risks_watch: Receivables: working capital cycle at 101 days; management says receivables normalise in Q1 FY27 with over three-quarters of Q4 receivables already collected. Watch the Q1 FY27 receivable run-rate.
US tariff regime and recovery: margins in the US remain below pre-tariff levels; watch whether volumes and margins improve each quarter from Q2 FY27.
Narmadapuram execution: commissioning slated for Q1 FY28 with EHV approvals expected by FY28; the 9-10% margin and INR 1,200 crore FY29 target depend on it.
Raw material (copper and aluminium) pass-through: policy is to avoid long firm-price orders, but EHV and longer-cycle orders may test this.
Management's FY31 INR 5,000 crore target and the FY27 guidance are informal and conditional on metal prices holding.

rows.why: IEEPA tariffs were invalidated by the US Supreme Court (Feb-Apr 2026) after rising to 50% in 2025, and management expects stronger US demand pull from Q2 FY27 after eight active US distributors (vs two in FY22) kept presence at sub-economic margins.

530555|2026-06.headline: Paramount Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore; operating margin (ex other income) expanded 320 bps YoY to 6.6%.
530555|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore but fell 7.7% QoQ, which management attributed to the seasonal Q4-to-Q1 pattern. Operating profit excluding other income rose 129.2% YoY to INR 34.7 crore, with margin up 320 bps YoY and 136 bps QoQ to 6.6%. The US export recovery after the IEEPA tariff invalidation drove exports to INR 155 crore (29%+ of revenue, up about 77% QoQ), while domestic revenue reached INR 374 crore. Order book rose to INR 615 crore from INR 583 crore, and a fresh equity raise of about INR 122 crore lifted net worth to INR 894 crore.

segments.name: Power cables
segments.commentary: Accounted for 57.2% of Q1 revenue; power cable order book INR 455 crore (about 74% of total orders), up 27% YoY.

segments.name: Domestic B2B industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 296 crore, up 92% YoY; management cites this higher-margin institutional mix as a margin driver.

segments.name: Exports (US-led)
segments.commentary: INR 155 crore in Q1, 29%+ of revenue; US distributors grew from 2 in FY22 to 8 now. Export order book only INR 97 crore.

segments.name: HTLS conductors
segments.commentary: Management cites INR 100 crore of business in hand; capacity build-out expected to be margin-accretive.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% YoY, constrained by existing plants running at effectively 100% utilisation.
EBITDA margin expected to return to FY25 levels (about 8% pre-tariff, per analyst framing) by Q4 FY27; operating margin of 6.6% is 'on track'.
FY27 US exports targeted at INR 700-800 crore, versus INR 155 crore in Q1.
Narmadapuram plant: partial commissioning in Q1 FY28; ~INR 500 crore revenue expected in FY28 and INR 1,200 crore by FY29 at 75% utilisation.
Long-term target of INR 5,000 crore revenue by FY31; management hopes to exceed it.
Working capital cycle to be kept within 90-100 days.
Debt-equity to stay below 0.3x after Narmadapuram phase 1, with a term loan planned later.
capex_capacity: Narmadapuram (Madhya Pradesh) is the third plant; phase 1 capex about INR 300 crore; about INR 30 crore+ spent so far; most critical machinery ordered; civil construction mobilised with 6-7 months expected for major works.
INR 65 crore of the equity raise earmarked for Narmadapuram; no debt drawn yet as of Q1.
Over the past 3-4 years, more than INR 155 crore spent on existing plants (Dharuhera, Khushkhera).

Approved up to 66 kV; 132 kV approvals expected to start within about a year of manufacturing start (one or two possibly in 6-8 months), with all approvals targeted by FY29. E-beam cables are a new product, with major certifications targeted by end-FY29.
Management is evaluating 220 kV and 400 kV products; not officially guided.
demand_pricing: Management describes demand as broad-based across power grid, renewables, data centres, railways/metro and construction; order inflows are firmer than anticipated at the start of the year.
US tariff regime normalised after the US Supreme Court invalidated IEEPA tariffs; management says India is now at par with other exporters.
Export order book is kept deliberately low (INR 97 crore) because firm-price orders are capped at 3-4 months delivery and most customers now bear tariff changes.
Key US competitors are South Korea, Vietnam and Cambodia, with Egypt, Ecuador and Turkey emerging. Management says the company faced 25%+ duty last year versus 10-18% for rivals.
Metal throughput up about 4% YoY (absolute figure not disclosed; last year's base cited as roughly 29,000 tons).
New US product: solar cables above 600 V; exports have started, with margins expected similar to current levels.
Existing plants are at effectively 100% utilisation; management says the constraint is manufacturing capacity, not demand.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins return to pre-tariff levels near 8%, and what drove the 320 bps YoY margin improvement and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is in line with expectations and FY25-level margins are targeted by at least Q4 FY27. Drivers cited: normalisation of US exports after the IEEPA duties were struck down (expected to add 300+ bps), and a higher-margin domestic power cable mix (~57% of Q1 revenue). Exports were 29%+ of revenue vs 15% in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Narmadapuram, and are there cost or time overruns?
qa_highlights.answer: Most critical machinery is ordered, with delivery lead times long but expected on time. Civil construction has started and major works are expected to take 6-7 months. Management does not expect major overruns. About INR 30 crore+ has been spent, plus more than INR 155 crore over three to four years on existing plants.

qa_highlights.question: How is Narmadapuram capex funded, and what utilisation supports the INR 1,200 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: No debt drawn yet; funding is from equity raised, internal accruals and planned term loan. Post phase 1, debt-equity is targeted below 0.3x. INR 1,200 crore is at 75% utilisation (the CFO-level comment referred to FY29). Approvals up to 66 kV are in place; 132 kV approvals are expected to start within about a year of manufacturing, with some possibly in 6-8 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the export order book only INR 97 crore despite strong export revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is deliberately keeping export orders low: firm-price orders are capped at 3-4 months delivery, and most customers now bear tariff changes. Management still expects INR 700-800 crore of US exports this year, versus INR 155 crore in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is current capacity utilisation, and what growth is possible in FY27 versus FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing plants run at practically 100% utilisation, and the constraint is manufacturing capacity rather than demand. FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20%. FY28 growth is expected to be much faster once Narmadapuram starts. The INR 5,000 crore FY31 target is seen as a floor to beat.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin progress at risk if H2 export mix falls, and how do export margins compare with domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export EBITDA was negative in FY26, about -4% to -4.5% at EBITDA level. Pre-FY26 export margins were about 1.5% above domestic. It said the company can pivot quickly between domestic and export, citing FY23 and FY25 shifts, and expects export margins to keep improving each quarter.

risks_watch: Narmadapuram execution: long machinery lead times, 6-7 month civil works, and a phase 1 capex of about INR 300 crore against INR 30 crore+ spent so far.
US tariff regime durability and export recovery: the target of INR 700-800 crore of exports versus a low export order book of INR 97 crore.
Margin path to FY25 levels (about 8% EBITDA) by Q4 FY27 from 6.6% operating margin; watch whether H2 export mix dilutes margins.
132 kV and EHV approvals timing (first approvals possibly 6-8 months after manufacturing starts; all by FY29) and E-beam certifications targeted by end-FY29.
Working capital: cash conversion cycle at 96 days versus the 90-100 day target; receivable days fell to 64 from 79.

Metal price and aluminium exposure: management says firm-price orders are capped at 3-4 months, but variable-price and +/- pass-through still carry some variation risk. Metal throughput was only disclosed as up about 4% YoY.
key_quotes: We delivered one of our strongest quarters on record, with healthy improvement across revenue, EBITDA, and profitability.

The 6.6% operating margin which excludes other income is quite a meaningful step for us to achieve the FY25 levels that we hope to close with in the current financial year, by atleast the last quarter of FY27.
Because, for Paramount the problem in is not selling, the problem is manufacturing, because our capacity has been constrained.
We do not expect to cross the level of 0.3x at best by the time we complete the first phase of our Narmadapuram project.

530555|2026-09.headline: Paramount Communications Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31.1% YoY to INR 560.4 crores, with operating margin at 7.3% versus 6.6% in Q1.
530555|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was INR 560.4 crores, up 31.1% YoY and 5.9% QoQ, with operating profit of INR 40.9 crores at a 7.3% margin. PAT was INR 24.2 crores (4.3% margin) and EPS INR 0.74. H1 FY27 revenue was INR 1,089.8 crores (up 24.1% YoY) with PAT of INR 43.9 crores. Management reiterated it expects to return to FY25 operating margins by Q4 FY27 and to reach roughly 8% operating margin around then, and it kept the Narmadapuram plant on schedule for partial commissioning in Q1 FY28.

financial_highlights.change: vs 6.6% in Q1 FY27 and 1.3% in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q2 exports were INR 158.1 crores (28.2% of revenue) and H1 exports INR 313.1 crores. Management expects US exports at 25-30% of FY27 revenue, with one analyst cited figure of INR 700 crores on this basis.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Q2 domestic revenue was INR 402.3 crores (71.8% of revenue). Power cables were 55.9% of revenue; B2B institutional INR 296.7 crores, B2C retail and distribution INR 53.7 crores, B2C government and PSU INR 51.9 crores.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: Order book at 30 Sep 2026 was INR 731 crores (domestic INR 632 crores, export INR 99 crores), including INR 575 crores of power cable and specialized conductor orders. HTLS order book was above INR 200 crores as of the call date.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% YoY (CFO-level range given as 15-18% for existing plants in one answer); H1 run rate described as indicative.

Operating margin to return to FY25 levels by Q4 FY27; about 8% operating margin targeted around Q4, excluding customer claw-backs, which are expected to show in Q3 results. Management said 'we are hopeful' on the 8% figure.

Narmadapuram plant: partial commissioning in Q1 FY28; revenue of about INR 500 crores in FY28 and INR 1,200 crores in FY29; capacity to double to about 60,000 MT over 3-4 years, with about 30,000 MT planned in that period.
Working capital: medium-term target 90-100 days, expected to normalize in H2 FY27.
Five-year target of INR 5,000 crores revenue by FY31, described as a guidance that will not be revised; management hopes to beat it.
Debt-equity expected to stay below 0.6-0.7 at most, and around 0.3 once the plant is operational. Long-term loans to be tied up in coming quarters for a INR 300 crore capex plan.
capex_capacity: Narmadapuram (Madhya Pradesh) greenfield plant, third facility: foundation and civil works under way; critical machinery ordered; partial commissioning expected Q1 FY28.

Narmadapuram scope: 220 kV AC power cable line, HTLS (carbon-core and gap-type), e-beam and rubber cables. Approvals take about 1-1.5 years for 220 kV, about 12 months for 132 kV, and 3-6 months for full 66 kV range after the plant is operational.
Existing Dharuhera and Khushkhera plants running at optimal utilization; some further capex planned at both to lift revenue.
Current capacity is about 30,000 MT; management plans to double it with the new plant.
demand_pricing: Management cites T&D investment, renewables, railways and metro, and data centers as multiyear demand drivers; the National Electricity Plan projects about INR 5 lakh crore of EHV transmission investment in 2027-2032.
Management sizes HTLS reconductoring at about INR 50,000 crore over 5 years; the company says it is among the top 5 HTLS players in India and offers up to 765 kV conductors.

Copper hit record highs in the quarter; aluminium (over 75% of metal value consumed) softened. Policy is to book metal the next working day after a firm-price order, and to avoid firm-price orders beyond 3-4 months.

US tariffs: IEEPA tariffs struck down by the US Supreme Court in February 2026; Indian cables now at par with Asian and European competitors. Most customers now carry tariff changes on their accounts.
Management says it is not chasing volume at the expense of margin; it is seeking approvals in Middle East, Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia, with results expected within 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin glide path, given export claw-backs and the tariff effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating margin went from 1.3% in Q2 FY26 to 3.3% in Q3 and 5.2% in Q4, then 6.6% in Q1 FY27 and 7.3% in Q2 FY27. Management expects domestic margins to matter more, with US exposure kept at about 30% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 8% margin target before or after claw-backs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 8% target is ex of claw-backs and that net claw-backs would be shown separately, visible in Q3. It was also said to be hopeful, not yet achieved, for Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is firm, and what is the cancellation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 731 crore order book comprises firm orders only, with very rare cancellations, and that even in the worst US period there were no major cancellations. It also said FY27 revenue visibility is comfortable given the H1 run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR 5,000 crore FY31 target be achieved sooner, and what margin goes with it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY31 is a conservative guidance it will not revise, but it hopes to beat it. It gave no EBITDA margin target for that revenue level.

qa_highlights.question: What are the approval timelines for the new plant's product ranges, and what revenue will come before 220 kV approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant will run on 11/33/66 kV orders from day one, with 132 kV approvals in about 12 months and 220 kV taking longer. It said the INR 500 crore FY28 and INR 1,200 crore FY29 targets will not be driven mainly by 220 kV in the first two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter B2C or face new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has no plans to enter the high-cost B2C segment. B2C house wire is about INR 100 crore of roughly INR 2,000 crore revenue, and it expects B2B to be unaffected by new entrants given its footprint.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 300 crore capex be funded, and what will leverage be?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said debt-equity is 0.14x now, with long-term loans to be tied up in coming quarters. Management expects debt-equity to stay around 0.3 after the plant is operational, and below 0.6-0.7 at most.

risks_watch: Metal price volatility, particularly copper and aluminium, and the company's ability to pass it through in 3-4 month order cycles.
Working capital at 108 days versus the 90-100 day target; management attributes this to early supplier payments and expects normalization in H2.
Narmadapuram execution: 220 kV approvals take 1-1.5 years, and FY28/FY29 revenue targets depend on ramp-up and product qualification.
Claw-back amounts and their timing, which could affect reported margins versus the 8% operating margin target.
Management's shift toward non-US export markets is at an early stage, with results expected in 1-2 years and substantial contribution in 2-3 years.
Management said the new plant's approvals and ramp-up could push the HTLS margin benefit later.
530555|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and the margin recovery, but cautious on specifics: management declined to give an EBITDA margin target and called the 8% operating margin goal 'hopeful' rather than assured. It was also evasive on HTLS technology and brand choices, saying those would not be discussed publicly.
key_quotes: When we last spoke in August, I said that we had started FY27 on a strong note and the two engines of our business, domestic and exports, were both working for us at the same time.
We are not chasing volume at the cost of margin and most of our customers now carry tariff changes to their account.
We do not accept firm-price orders with long delivery periods beyond 3 to 4 months because that is how we protect ourselves from metal volatility.
We have not achieved. It's not happened, but we can say that we are hopeful, yes.

rows.why: Narmadapuram greenfield plant (INR 300 crore capex) is under construction with partial commissioning guided for Q1 FY28, taking capacity from ~30,000 MT toward ~60,000 MT over 3-4 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% YoY, H1 FY27 revenue was up 24.1% YoY, and the order book stands at INR 731 crore including INR 575 crore of power cable and conductor orders.

rows.why: Management said some further capex is planned at Dharuhera and Khushkhera, but no size or timing was given beyond the INR 300 crore Narmadapuram plan, and utilisation is described only as 'optimal' with no figure.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it hopes to beat the INR 5,000 crore FY31 target and that FY27 revenue visibility is comfortable, but it held FY27 growth at 15-20% and called the 8% margin only hopeful.
