rows.why: Claw-back amounts are due to show in Q3 results, working capital at 108 days versus a 90-100 day target, and 220 kV approvals take 1-1.5 years, which could slip the margin and FY28-FY29 revenue targets.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Narmadapuram will produce 220 kV AC power cable, HTLS (carbon-core and gap-type), e-beam and rubber cables, with 11/33/66 kV orders from day one and 132 kV approvals in about 12 months.

rows.label: Non-US export approvals (Middle East, Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia)
rows.why: Management is seeking approvals in these regions with results expected within 1-2 years and substantial contribution in 2-3 years, while US exports are guided at INR 700 crore or 25-30% of FY27 revenue.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation to 90-100 days
rows.why: Net working capital days rose to 108 from 101 at end FY26 against a 90-100 day target, and management expects normalisation in H2 FY27.

rows.label: Debt-equity stays low after the plant
rows.why: Debt-equity is 0.14x now, with long-term loans for the INR 300 crore capex to be tied up in coming quarters and management expects it to stay around 0.3 once the plant is operational.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the order book and FY27 growth of 15-20%, but cautious on the 8% margin target, calling it 'hopeful', and declined to give an EBITDA margin target; analysts pressed on margin glide path, claw-backs, and order book firmness.

530655|2026-03.headline: Goodluck India Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin above 10% and PAT up 34% YoY to over INR56 crore, while FY27 growth guidance was trimmed to 14-15%.
530655|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was about INR1,097 crore, with management citing EBITDA margins above 10% and PAT up 34% YoY to over INR56 crore. Standalone Q4 sales fell to INR1,061.46 crore from INR1,104.62 crore, while standalone Q4 EBITDA rose 11.7% to INR104.19 crore. FY26 revenue growth of about 4% to 5% fell well short of the earlier 15-20% guidance, which management blamed on lower HRC prices and the West Asia conflict disrupting dispatches. Defence (artillery shells) began production in Jan-Feb 2026 after licensing in October 2025 and contributed about INR46 crore revenue and INR29 crore EBITDA in FY26, a margin inflated by start-up depreciation and interest per management.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1,104.62 crore in Q4 FY25 (down about 4%)

financial_highlights.value: about INR1,000 crore (working capital loans INR800 crore, term loan INR200 crore), cash and bank about INR50 crore
INR340 crore per analyst; management said capex/WIP about INR232 crore

segments.name: Defence (artillery shells, Goodluck Defence)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR46 crore and EBITDA about INR29 crore; capacity 150,000 shells with 75-80% execution targeted in FY27 (INR250-300 crore revenue indicated). Capacity expansion to 400,000 shells is planned at about INR400 crore capex, not yet started.

segments.name: Steel / legacy businesses
segments.commentary: Management cited FY26 production growth of about 11% against sales growth of about 5%, and 94% overall capacity utilisation. Standalone capacity is about 5 lakh tonnes, with a target of 6 lakh tonnes within 9-12 months.

segments.name: Hydraulic tubes (construction equipment)
segments.commentary: Utilisation was about 50% in FY26, targeted at 65-70% in FY27 with the ramp-up in progress.

segments.name: Solar structures and GI conduit / front fork tubes
segments.commentary: Solar sales rose 33% in FY26 with utilisation still low. Conduit pipe EBITDA guided at 15-20% (mainly US exports) and front fork tubes at 15-16%, with 35,000-45,000 tonnes of added capacity in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 14-15% (earlier 15-20%), with management hopeful but conditional on West Asia conflict easing.
Defence EBITDA margin guided at 30-35% once volumes are sufficient, though management said FY26's margin was not sustainable.
Gross margin said to be sustainable (analyst cited about 27-28% to about 33% YoY improvement).

guidance_outlook: Domestic: management is targeting about 10% organisation-level volume growth in FY27, and expects a further 2–3% improvement in average domestic realisation in Q1 FY27 versus about INR79,000–80,000 per MT in Q4.

Exports: no numeric guidance; management said April ran in line with Q4 trajectory, while May and June were still unclear. It expects exports to rebound sharply once the Middle East conflict settles, and said the recent lost volumes could be recovered in three to four months after settlement.
Inventory: 530,000 tonnes of rice-equivalent stock at 31 Mar 2026. Management expects to build inventory in the coming season, depending on crop and pricing, and sees the export demand as strong.
Edible oil: expects healthy double-digit growth in FY27.
Real estate: Samalkha (Panipat) land parcel of about 130 acres; the 60-acre portion is earmarked for own warehousing near Sonipat/Barota, and no monetisation decision has been taken.

Rice-equivalent inventory of about 530,000 tonnes against FY26 sales of about 560,000 MT domestic and 160,000 MT export.
Distribution: 3.4 lakh retail outlets, 16 C&F agents and 8 super stockists; supply chain shift towards an FOR model.
Samalkha land parcel (about 130 acres, split by GT road): the 60-acre side is for KRBL's own warehousing given space constraints at the Barota plant.
demand_pricing: Domestic branded basmati: Q4 realisation about INR79,000–80,000 per MT; price stabilisation and brand investment supported growth, while Q3 domestic revenue was flat YoY on competitive and pricing pressure.

Market share in packaged basmati (FY26): general trade 36.9%, modern trade 38.7%, e-commerce 40.1%. Management said Q4 share was 100–200 bps higher than the full-year level in each channel; it did not give a YoY comparison for Q4.

Exports: Middle East shipments were hit in March 2026. Cargo has largely reached destinations since April–May. Alternate routes (Khor Fakkan, Jeddah, Salalah, Jordan for Iraq) carry higher freight, insurance and transit times. Management reports Saudi business is continuing.

Industry: India's FY26 basmati exports rose about 8% to 6.5 million MT (record); non-basmati exports about 15 million MT (+6%). Pakistan Super Basmati has traded at a premium to Indian 1121 since October 2025 (USD1,180–1,220/MT FOB).
Global: USDA sees 2026-27 global rice production at about 538 million MT versus 543 million MT, with consumption rising to about 541 million MT. Management said this could keep prices firm.

qa_highlights.question: Export run-rate: how much further decline versus Q4 in Q1, and April numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no April or monthly export figures and said Q1 depends on the geopolitical situation. Ashish said April was 'in the same trajectory' as Q4, with May and June still to be seen.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory build-up for FY27 and the competitive environment in exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Anoop Gupta said inventory will be built in the coming season, depending on crop and pricing. Management cited a 8–9% margin on unsold stock and about 35–40 tonnes of export rice at Kandla (about 20% cheaper than current prices), which could be sold domestically.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic volume growth and whether Q4 can be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 10% organisation-level domestic volume growth in FY27; Q4 volume growth was 16%.

qa_highlights.question: Use of about INR1,000 crore cash: special dividend or buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish said only the approved INR103 crore dividend (450%) was in scope; no other capital return measures were announced.

qa_highlights.question: Real estate: why not monetise the Samalkha land and what about the buyback question?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60-acre portion will be used for own warehousing despite the higher profit from a sale. It is evaluating opportunities but will only invest in real estate if the return could double the investment.

qa_highlights.question: Basmati price outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to comment, as the India Rice Exporters' Association crop-size contract is still being mapped; a view on FY27 pricing awaits the crop size.

qa_highlights.question: Saudi distributor appointment and channel inventory in exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is staying selective and direct with wholesalers in Saudi Arabia; no distributor has been appointed. Ashish declined to quantify channel inventory but said most Middle East markets are below normal stock levels.

530813|2026-06.headline: KRBL Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR261 crores (16.7% margin) on price hikes and investment gains, while exports fell about 50% on Middle East disruption.
530813|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue for operations was INR1,496 crores, down about 6% YoY, as Middle East exports collapsed to INR244 crores (from INR485 crores) after the Strait of Hormuz disruption. Exports to all other regions grew 37%. Domestic revenue excluding power rose 14% to INR1,221 crores, driven by about 9-11% higher realisations, while branded bulk-pack volumes declined. Gross margin (including other income) jumped to 36.3% from 25.7%, and EBITDA margin to 23.8% from 13.9%, helped by INR64 crores of other income including MTM and forex gains. Management called the margins unsustainable and guided FY27 to about 30% gross margin and 17-18% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Export - Middle East
segments.commentary: Exports to the Middle East fell sharply, driving total export revenue down about 50% to INR244 crores; management attributes the decline entirely to route closure and freight costs.

segments.name: Export - other regions
segments.commentary: Exports to all other regions grew 37% in the quarter, per management.

segments.name: Domestic (India business)
segments.commentary: Domestic revenue excluding power rose 14% to INR1,221 crores; consumer pack and regional rice performed well, while branded bulk-pack volumes declined on timing of purchases. Modern trade rice volume grew 6.5% and value 13%; e-commerce primary sales grew about 50%.

segments.name: Masala and regional rice
segments.commentary: Masala portfolio grew 74% in value YoY with an annualised run rate of about INR9 crores, targeting INR25 crores by FY27-end. Branded regional rice grew 25%, against a base of about INR270 crores in FY26.

Export shortfall described as timing; export volumes expected to recover progressively from Q2 and meaningful full-year export growth maintained.

Basmati export volume about 1.5 million tons vs 1.7 million tons in Q1 FY26; Middle East volumes down about 11% YoY.
Container freight from west coast India to Middle East rose from about US$500 to as much as US$5,000 per container at peak.
Pakistani basmati priced about USD100 per ton above comparable Indian material; Pakistan rice exports for year to June 2026 fell about 26% in volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Saudi Arabia entity, and are direct bookings continuing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is searching for a distributor after past problems with a wrong partner; 3-4 candidates identified, with finalisation awaiting peace in the region. The direct entity programme is deferred, while wholesaler shipments continue.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 exports be higher, and can restocking absorb high freight costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gulf benchmark prices have risen, letting it pass on freight costs; Q2 export numbers expected to be much better, though container space and equipment shortages are slowing movement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 margins are not sustainable; FY27 guidance is about 30% gross margin and 17-18% EBITDA margin, versus about 15% last year.

qa_highlights.question: How will domestic volume grow, and what is the regional/quick commerce plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 10% domestic volume growth for the next 2-3 years; Q1 volume dip was due to deferred bulk-pack orders. More regional rice varieties will be listed on quick commerce platforms later this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why not buy more inventory given available cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will buy more paddy this season, but purchases depend on market conditions; current stock of 389,000 tons of rice is considered comfortable.

qa_highlights.question: What are the regional rice and overall revenue targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Regional rice is targeted to grow 25% on about INR270 crores; overall guidance is about 10% volume growth, with price guidance withheld because of West Asia uncertainty and the upcoming paddy season.

qa_highlights.question: Will basmati prices rise if the Gulf supply gap reopens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices would rise if peace returns, but the size of the new crop is uncertain after late rains; crop size clarity expected around 25 August.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gross margin structurally sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 gross margin is not sustainable, driven by price increases and MTM gains; FY27 gross margin guided at about 30%.

530813|2026-09.headline: KRBL Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR1,727 crore (+14% YoY) on a 33% domestic surge, while exports fell 41% in H1 on Middle East disruption.
530813|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was KRBL's highest-ever quarterly revenue, driven by domestic branded consumer packs (volume +18% YoY per management, with a later +19% figure) and a selective INR102 crore bulk rice sale. Exports remained the weak spot: H1 export revenue was INR541 crore (-41%), almost entirely from bulk exports to the Middle East, though Q2 exports rose 22% QoQ to INR297 crore. PAT was INR159 crore (14.6% margin) versus INR172 crore (11.2%) a year earlier, and cash plus treasury investments rose to INR2,895 crore. Management guided Q3 EBITDA of 16-20% and FY27 EBITDA of 17-19%, with paddy prices up sharply for the new crop.

If the US-Iran situation settles, bulk exports could more than double, with management citing 30,000-40,000 tons or more; Iran previously ~100,000 tons a year.

qa_highlights.question: What export and volume growth is expected from here, and would exports double if the US-Iran situation settles?
qa_highlights.answer: Anil Mittal said exports could more than double once a US-Iran agreement is reached, with bulk sales (near zero in H1) possibly reaching 30,000-40,000 tons or more. Ayush Gupta reiterated about 10% domestic volume growth for the year.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected in Q3 given the low-cost inventory and higher paddy prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Anoop Gupta guided Q3 EBITDA of 16-20%, saying old-crop stock earns higher margins and new-crop margins will be lower; he later said the figure would be nearing 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 vs Q1 volume growth, and why did gross margin fall from 33.5% to 32.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Jain cited 18% QoQ rice volume growth and 18% QoQ domestic growth, and attributed the margin dip to lower forex and treasury gains in other income, with higher freight and advertising costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation for domestic and export sales and the Q3 price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic realisation was about INR80/kg and exports about INR132/kg. Management said Q3 domestic prices would be about 7-8% higher on average, after earlier citing 15-18% increases.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue reach about INR7,500 crore with a 16-17% PAT margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Jain said H1 revenue was about INR3,200 crore. He said the scenario looks feasible only if H2 exports recover to at least the prior year's roughly INR1,550 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are quick commerce contribution, the Middle East outlook, and capital return plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce is 8-9% of India business with a 41.1% share. Anoop Gupta said a buyback could be considered and the company would discuss it internally. The dividend policy is 15% of profit, with management indicating it could exceed that.

Procurement: paddy procurement planned at about 750,000 tons for FY27, with paddy prices up about 20% YoY (Anoop Gupta); buying staggered across the season with focus on low moisture, high recovery paddy.
Inventory at 30 Sep 2026: paddy 31,000 tons (vs 33,000 tons a year earlier) and rice 278,000 tons (vs 304,000 tons); management said inventory extends about one and a half years for some SKUs.

Distribution: India Gate present in about 3.3 lakh outlets and reaches about 1.2 crore urban households; order-to-cash programme under way to link order placement, stock allocation, collections and claims; work on availability in under-penetrated towns.
Export go-to-market: management decided against opening its own office in Saudi Arabia, preferring distributors; Africa (South Africa) cited as a growth area.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 consumer pack volume growth was 18% YoY (Ayush Gupta later gave 19% YoY for Q2 rice volumes); Q1 was 7%. Modern trade and e-commerce consumer pack volumes +31%; general trade +10% after about 5% decline in Q1. Bulk packs +11% YoY in Q2, October described as another strong month; regional rice +42% in Q2, +32% in H1.

Domestic realisation about INR80/kg in both Q1 and Q2 FY27, about 12% higher than Q2 FY26. Export realisation about INR132/kg in Q2. Price increases taken across the portfolio in Q3: management said 7-8% on average, after earlier citing 15-18% on specific price points.

Market share (12 months to September): India Gate about 36% in general trade (nearly twice the next player), 39.6% in modern trade, and internal estimate of 41.1% in e-commerce exit share in September versus about 33% for the next player; quick commerce is 8-9% of the India business.

Export demand: H1 bulk exports to the Middle East near zero; branded exports +18% in H1; non-Middle East exports +14% in H1. Management said Saudi Arabia steady; Iran shut for banking reasons after August US sanctions; if the US-Iran situation settles, bulk exports could rise more than double, with 30,000-40,000 tons or more cited. Management also cited Iran's earlier level of about 100,000 tons a year.

Global and Indian basmati context: basmati paddy trading at INR4,500-5,200 per quintal, with 1509 and 1121 varieties up at least INR1,000 per quintal YoY; non-basmati prices up about 30%; FY27 export volumes for India basmati Apr-Aug at 2.5 million tons vs 2.7 million tons a year earlier, with realisations about 21% higher in rupee terms.

Guidance: domestic rice volume growth of about 10% for FY27 (H2 focus), with management saying the 19% Q2 rate is not a promise; FY27 exports expected to match or beat the prior year's roughly INR1,500-1,550 crore; FY27 EBITDA 17-19%; Q3 EBITDA 16-20%, with management later saying it would be nearing 20%.

rows.why: Q3 EBITDA guided at 16-20% (nearing 20%) versus 21.1% in Q2, with 7-8% Q3 price increases offset by paddy inflation of about 20% and lower treasury gains; FY27 EBITDA guided at 17-19%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets about 10% domestic rice volume growth for FY27 (H2-weighted) after 18-19% in Q2 and 7% in Q1, backed by 36% general-trade share and modern trade/e-commerce volume +31%, though management said the 19% Q2 rate is not a promise.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or capacity expansion was discussed on the call; the brief lists capex_read as not discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said FY27 exports could match or beat roughly INR1,500-1,550 crore and bulk exports could more than double if US-Iran settles (30,000-40,000 tons cited), but this depends on Gulf developments.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Exports (H1 INR541 crore, -41%) hinge on Gulf conditions, and paddy prices up about 20% YoY could compress margins as new-crop costs flow through, against FY27 EBITDA guidance of 17-19%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Masala ambition to exit FY27 at an annualised run rate of about INR25 crore, versus H1 sales of about INR4.5 crore; no new product launches were named.

rows.label: Q3 domestic price increase of 7-8%
rows.why: Price increases were taken across the portfolio in Q3, averaging 7-8% after earlier citing 15-18% on specific price points, against paddy prices up about 20% YoY.

rows.label: Possible buyback
rows.why: Anoop Gupta said a buyback could be considered and would be discussed internally, with no decision given; dividend policy is 15% of profit and could exceed that.

rows.label: Africa (South Africa) export growth
rows.why: Management cited Africa as a growth area and chose distributors over an own Saudi office, but gave no volume or revenue figures.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic volume, share and pricing, but cautious on exports, which it tied to Gulf and US-Iran developments; analysts pressed on Q3 margin range, FY27 revenue/PAT scenario, and buyback response, which were answered with ranges or hedges.

530999|2026-03.headline: Balaji Amines Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 12% YoY to INR403 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25% versus 19% a year earlier.
530999|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR403 crore (up about 12% YoY) and EBITDA was INR102 crore against INR68 crore, lifting margin to 25% from 19% in Q4 FY25 and 18% in Q3 FY26. PAT reached INR65 crore versus INR40 crore a year earlier. Management said production was briefly hit in March 2026 by a geopolitical situation but was managed through inventory planning. For FY27 management guided to 10-15% consolidated volume growth in Q&A, and to 20-30% volume growth and 22-23% EBITDA margin by end-FY27 (wording varied during the call). Specialty subsidiary Balaji Specialty Chemicals was running partially during modifications, which depressed its quarterly margins.

segments.name: Amines
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 7,746 MT. Management said DMF and butylamines run at low utilisation as battery-chemical demand has yet to ramp.

segments.name: Amines derivatives
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 8,935 MT; described as a stable operating base.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 10,660 MT. Subsidiary Balaji Specialty Chemicals ran only about 10-20 days a month during modifications, and management said Q4 subsidiary margins are not a usable benchmark.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume growth of 10-15% (Q&A, for this year), with 20-30% volume growth cited for the period to end-FY27 once new plants ramp.
EBITDA margin expected to be sustainable at 22-23% of sales (stated for end-FY27).
Management targets INR3,000 crore revenue in FY28 (said to be reached in 2028); an earlier-cited INR2,000 crore target was referenced by an analyst.
DME plant at Unit 4 expected to commission in Q1 FY27; utilisation of 30-40% in FY27, 50-60% by year-end, and 80-90% in the following year, subject to road transport permission.
Balaji Specialty Chemicals Unit-I (EDA-based DETA, TETA, PIP, AEEA, AEP) expected in H1 FY27; Unit-II Chincholi (HCN, NaCN, EDTA, EDTA-2Na) expected in Q4 FY27.

Standalone capex remaining for DME, NMM and ACN is about INR20 crore; subsidiary capex about INR275-290 crore consolidated this year (INR200-250 crore subsidiary spend). Phase 1 of the INR750 crore expansion is INR350-400 crore.
capex_capacity: Standalone capacity cited by an analyst at 2,93,000 MT; an analyst estimated utilisation at 35-40%, which management did not dispute.
NMM project of 5,000 TPA under execution, commissioning during FY27; improved-process Acetonitrile (ACN) plant to commission in Q2 FY27.
DME plant at Unit 4 (about 1 lakh tonne capacity) ready to commission; road transport permission awaited, expected in about a month per management.
Balaji Specialty Chemicals expansion of about INR750 crore in phases, Maharashtra Mega Project status under Package Scheme of Incentives 2019.
Battery chemicals unit is running at 20-25% capacity, with production also going to agro and pharma uses.
demand_pricing: Management said raw material costs were up to 2-3x normal in some cases; monoethanolamine was cited at about 3x normal.
EDA/DETA prices averaged about INR300/kg in Q4 and were INR270-280 currently, per management.
Indicative prices: DME about INR100-120/kg, ACN about INR240, NMM about INR250-300.
A large metformin customer that backward-integrated still buys DMA-HCl; management put it at 15-20% of outflow for that product.
Ammonia and methanol available; prices volatile, with purchases now made in shorter lots every 3-4 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand with standalone utilisation around 35-40%, and which products are low-utilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new projects are new products, not capacity adds for existing lines. Low utilisation is in DMF, butylamines and battery chemicals (DMC) because battery demand has not started.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike was taken in Q4 and what realisation growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers accepted price increases in Q4 and margins were held through inventory management. Guidance: 20-30% volume growth and 22-23% EBITDA margin by end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR2,000 crore to INR3,000 crore FY28 target realistic given DME approvals and slow specialty demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DME manufacturing permissions are in place and only transport approval is pending. It reaffirmed INR3,000 crore revenue in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary other expenses drop and what are subsidiary raw material trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiary worked about 10-15 days a month during modifications, with repair costs partly capitalised. Monoethanolamine costs were about 3x normal. Management said the quarter was not a benchmark and asked analysts to email the company secretary for modelling inputs.

qa_highlights.question: What is remaining standalone capex and FY27 subsidiary capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone balance is about INR20 crore. Subsidiary spend is about INR200-250 crore this year after INR110 crore already spent, for total consolidated capex of INR275-290 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will DME be sold before transport permission arrives and what volume is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Samples went out in 500 kg cylinders for trials, and bulk orders follow permission. Management said FY27 utilisation would be marginal, with 60-70% growth next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company increase its stake in BSE, and what is the status of the greenfield project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stake increase needs both boards and shareholders, and an IPO is not yet decided. On capex, it said modifications at the subsidiary began last year, and it plans to invite investors to a plant visit around June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of antidumping duties on DMF and EDA?
qa_highlights.answer: No DMF application has been filed, and the old case remains. The EDA case was at final stage, but duty exemptions run to end-June, so the outcome is pending.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: ammonia, methanol and monoethanolamine prices and supply are moving every few days, and management said margin holds depend on this.
Battery chemicals demand (DMC, DMF, electrolytes) has not ramped, and a plant running at 20-25% is still dependent on a customer start.
DME commissioning depends on road transport permission and the first-time product market acceptance; management guides to 30-40% FY27 utilisation.
Subsidiary Balaji Specialty Chemicals is partly idle during modifications, so its quarterly numbers are not clean; watch Q1 and Q2 FY27 ramp-up.
Antidumping duty decisions on EDA and DMF are pending; government exemptions run to end-June 2026.
Management guidance was inconsistent on FY27 volume growth (10-15% vs 20-30%) and on the FY28 revenue target (INR2,000 crore vs INR3,000 crore).
530999|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on margins and the expansion pipeline, but vague and inconsistent on numbers: it gave a 10-15% FY27 volume range in one answer and 20-30% in another, and declined to give price-hike quantum or DME revenue timing. Tone turned defensive when analysts questioned the INR3,000 crore FY28 target and subsidiary performance.
key_quotes: Our consolidated EBITDA for Q4 FY26 stood at INR102 crores as compared to INR68 crores in Q4 FY25.
We will be definitely reaching INR3,000 crores in 2028.
Consolidated debt stood at INR133 crores, mainly on account of ongoing expansion related activities.

rows.why: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin rose to 25% from 19% a year earlier and 18% in Q3 FY26, and management guides 22-23% sustainable by end-FY27, but raw material costs are 2-3x normal (monoethanolamine about 3x) and the subsidiary is partly idle, so Q4's 25% is not a clean run-rate.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided FY27 consolidated volume growth of 10-15% (Q4 FY26 volume was 27,341 MT, up from 25,871 MT, about 6% YoY), with DME utilisation 30-40% in FY27 and 50-60% by year-end, but growth is contingent on DME permission and battery-chemical customer start.

rows.why: Standalone utilisation is about 35-40%, far below the 80%+ threshold, so a fresh capacity announcement is not forced; however the Balaji Specialty phased INR750 crore expansion is being raised with INR350-400 crore Phase 1 and consolidated FY27 capex of INR275-290 crore, and a plant visit for investors is planned around June.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 volume growth to 10-15% and standalone utilisation is only 35-40%, with battery chemicals at 20-25% and DMF and butylamines at low utilisation, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.why: FY27 volume guidance was cut from 25-30% to 10-15% in the Q&A, and guidance was inconsistent (20-30% cited for end-FY27), with subsidiary running only 10-20 days a month and monoethanolamine costs about 3x normal.

rows.why: DME (Unit 4) is ready to commission in Q1 FY27 with bulk sales after transport permission, NMM in FY27, ACN in Q2 FY27, Specialty Unit-I (DETA, TETA, PIP, AEEA, AEP) in H1 FY27 and Unit-II (HCN, NaCN, EDTA) in Q4 FY27.

rows.label: DME utilisation ramp after transport permission
rows.why: Samples have gone out in 500 kg cylinders and bulk orders follow permission, with management guiding 30-40% FY27 utilisation on about 1 lakh tonne capacity, but permission is still awaited and no DME revenue timing was given.

rows.label: Antidumping duty decisions on EDA and DMF
rows.why: EDA case is at final stage but duty exemptions run to end-June, and no DMF application has been filed, so outcome is pending and could move EDA and DMF pricing.

rows.label: Stake increase in Balaji Specialty / possible IPO
rows.why: Management said the stake increase needs both boards and shareholders and an IPO is not yet decided, so no near-term corporate action is firm.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, DME permissions and the expansion pipeline, but vague and inconsistent on FY27 volume (10-15% vs 20-30%) and went defensive when analysts questioned the INR3,000 crore FY28 target and subsidiary performance.

530999|2026-09.headline: Balaji Amines Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36% YoY to INR472 crores and PAT 82% to INR67 crores, though EBITDA fell sequentially to INR106 crores.
530999|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR472 crores, up about 36% YoY and up from INR461 crores in Q1, while EBITDA was INR106 crores (22% margin) versus INR121 crores (26%) in Q1. Sales volume rose about 13.5% QoQ to 24,491 MT but was down about 6% YoY. H1 FY27 PAT was INR146 crores, up about 98%, despite H1 volumes falling to 46,078 MT from 53,735 MT. The company commissioned the expanded Acetonitrile plant (1,440 TPM) and the DME plant, and it received PESO approval for DME road tanker valves; brownfield and greenfield specialty chemicals projects have slipped toward FY27 end and Q4 FY27 respectively.

segments.name: Amines (volume)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume of 6,525 MT. Unit-4 methylamine utilisation is only about 15-20% per management, while Unit-3 ran at about 80%.

segments.name: Amines Derivatives (volume)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume of 8,974 MT. DMF plant utilisation rose from about 30-40% to more than 50% on DMF prices of INR110-115 per kg. EDA utilisation is about 50-60%.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals (volume)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume of 8,992 MT. DME and Acetonitrile are ramping; Acetonitrile is priced around INR230-240 per kg.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to reach INR3,500-4,000 crores top line by FY28-29, which the analyst had framed as a INR3,000-4,000 crore aspiration.
All expansions, including Acetonitrile, DME, DMF, NMM and the Balaji Specialty Chemicals projects, are to be completed by end of FY27. From Q1 FY28, the focus shifts to utilisation of 80-90%.

Unit-1 brownfield at Balaji Specialty Chemicals (EDA derivatives) is expected to be commissioned by end FY27. Unit-2 greenfield at Chincholi (hydrogen cyanide, sodium cyanide, EDTA) is targeted for Q4 FY27, with some products possibly slipping to February or March 2027.
NMM commercialisation is targeted during FY27.

DME: bulk supply is expected once Road Tanker approval is received (3-4 weeks) and the BPCL LPG-blending approval is in place. Capacity utilisation could exceed 90% with that approval, or 50-55% without it.
Acetonitrile: full capacity of 1,440 MT per month expected in 2-3 weeks; management guided minimum 1,000-1,200 MT per month from December, subject to market acceptance.
DME pricing indicated at INR90-100 per kg currently, expected to be competitive with LPG once methanol falls below INR80 per kg.
capex_capacity: Expanded Acetonitrile plant commenced commercial production in Q2 FY27 at 1,440 tons per month capacity, with improved process technology.
DME plant commissioned; PESO approval received for DME road tanker valves. Road tanker approval expected in 3-4 weeks. 7-8 ISO tanks exported for aerosol use; about 20-25 cylinders sold domestically.

Unit-1 at Balaji Specialty Chemicals (brownfield EDA derivatives: DETA, TETA, Piperazine, AEEA, AEP) is being run in 10-15 day cycles alternating with modifications. Remaining work is small equipment erection, to finish in one or two cycles by January 2027.
Unit-2 greenfield at MIDC Chincholi is in equipment erection and installation, targeted for Q4 FY27.

Di-isopropylamine process improvement reported as yielding positive results. Management also cited a DMC/DMC-PC order from a battery electrolyte client for 500-1,000 MT, with delivery expected from next month.
demand_pricing: Volumes lag because raw material prices are volatile, so the company is booking orders against demand rather than building inventory. H1 FY27 volume fell about 14% YoY.
DMF prices rose to INR110-115 per kg from earlier levels. Management said Chinese dumping had previously made Indian DMF uneconomic.
EDA price improved, but anti-dumping duty recommended by the Commerce Ministry was not implemented by the Finance Ministry. The company plans a High Court writ petition within about one month.
Methanol is about INR61-62 per kg versus INR6 when management began the business. Management expects normal levels of INR26-30. Ammonia is INR80-90 versus a normal INR45-50.
DME demand is mainly aerosol in India (over 50,000 tons consumption) and export; LPG blending is pending BPCL and government approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the DMF plant now that DMF prices have risen, and when will Unit-4 methylamine improve?
qa_highlights.answer: DMF utilisation has risen from about 30-40% to more than 50% at prices above INR110-115 per kg. Unit-3 ran near 80%. Unit-4 is at about 15-20% and management expects 70-80% over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on DMC supply to the battery electrolyte client and on any further capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: The client now asks for 500-1,000 MT of DMC and propylene carbonate, against earlier requests of 20-60 MT. Delivery is expected from next month. Further capacity depends on other clients coming on stream; no decision yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EDA volume not picking up after anti-dumping, and what is the next step?
qa_highlights.answer: EDA is running at about 50-60% utilisation. The Commerce Ministry recommended anti-dumping duty but the Finance Ministry did not implement it. The company plans a writ petition in the High Court within about one month.

qa_highlights.question: What approvals remain for DME LPG blending, and what pricing should be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Valves approval is done. Road tanker approval is expected in 3-4 weeks, followed by BPCL and government approval for LPG blending. Current DME pricing is INR90-100 per kg, which management expects to become competitive below methanol at INR80.

qa_highlights.question: What Acetonitrile pricing should be assumed, and what is the value growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Acetonitrile is at about INR230-240 per kg and depends on raw material prices. Full capacity is expected in 2-3 weeks. Management reiterated INR3,500-4,000 crore top line by FY28-29 even if prices decline.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Unit-1 brownfield expansion been delayed from July, then October, to year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company keeps the plant running to serve the market and cannot run manufacturing and expansion in the same plant at once. Products should reach the market from January 2027, with possible slippage to February or March.

risks_watch: Brownfield timelines have slipped repeatedly (July 2026, then October 2026, then FY27 end). Unit-1 and Unit-2 commissioning could slip to February-March 2027.
Volumes have fallen YoY, and utilisation is low at Unit-4 methylamine (15-20%), EDA (50-60%) and the existing DMC capacity (about 30%).
The EDA anti-dumping duty stalled at the Finance Ministry, and the company's High Court petition timing is uncertain.
Raw material price volatility (methanol, ammonia) and geopolitical conditions drive pricing for DME, Acetonitrile and DMF. Management said prices could fall once conditions normalise.
Sequential EBITDA margin fell from 26% to 22%. The DME LPG-blending approval is still pending.
Net worth figure was corrected on the call from INR2,023.02 crores to INR2,083.02 crores, so the transcript figure needs confirming.
530999|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on profitability and the expansion narrative, but cautious and at times evasive on timelines and volumes. Management repeatedly cited regulatory and logistics delays, and it deferred the DME pricing and approval questions to uncertain external approvals.

rows.why: Acetonitrile guided to a minimum 1,000-1,200 MT/month from December, DMC order of 500-1,000 MT from next month, and DMF utilisation up from 30-40% to above 50%, against H1 FY27 volume down about 14% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is low at Unit-4 methylamine (15-20%), EDA (50-60%) and DMC (about 30%), so near-term new capex is unlikely, but management's INR3,500-4,000 crore top-line target for FY28-29 implies further investment after the FY27 projects are complete.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated INR3,500-4,000 crore top line by FY28-29 (versus INR933 crore in H1 FY27, up 31% YoY), though the call framed it as an aspiration and the figure was raised from a prior analyst framing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Brownfield and greenfield timelines have slipped repeatedly, Unit-1/Unit-2 could slip to February-March 2027, and DME at 50-55% utilisation without LPG-blending approval, which is still pending.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Unit-1 EDA derivatives (DETA, TETA, piperazine, AEEA, AEP) are expected to reach market from January 2027, Unit-2 products (hydrogen cyanide, sodium cyanide, EDTA) in Q4 FY27, and NMM commercialisation is targeted during FY27.

rows.label: EDA anti-dumping duty via High Court writ
rows.why: Commerce Ministry recommended anti-dumping duty but Finance Ministry did not implement it; company plans a High Court writ within about one month, and EDA utilisation is only 50-60%.

rows.label: DME LPG-blending and road tanker approvals
rows.why: Road tanker approval expected in 3-4 weeks; DME utilisation could exceed 90% with BPCL LPG-blending approval versus 50-55% without it, at DME pricing of INR90-100/kg.

rows.label: Methanol and ammonia normalisation
rows.why: Methanol at INR61-62/kg vs normal INR26-30 and ammonia at INR80-90 vs normal INR45-50; a fall would lift margins but could also cut DMF, DME and Acetonitrile prices.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability, the INR3,500-4,000 crore top-line target and Acetonitrile/DME ramp, but cautious and at times evasive on brownfield timelines, volumes and pending DME and EDA approvals; analysts pressed on timing slippage and utilisation.

531120|2026-03.headline: Patel Engineering FY26 revenue INR 5,103 crore (flat YoY); FY27 guided to grow 10% with order book at INR 15,119 crore.
531120|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 5,102 crore versus INR 5,093 crore in FY25, with PAT up 21% to INR 294 crore. Q4 consolidated revenue was INR 1,421 crore with operating EBITDA of INR 215 crore (15.14% margin) and PAT of INR 71.5 crore versus INR 32.8 crore a year earlier. Gross debt fell to INR 1,187 crore from INR 1,645 crore after the rights issue, and debt-to-equity improved to 0.27 from 0.43. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of about 10%, with momentum expected to build from H2 FY27, and expects about INR 8,000 crore of new orders in FY27.

segments.name: Hydropower
segments.commentary: 55% of FY26 revenue and 63% of order book at 31 Mar 2026; Subansiri Lower has four of eight units running (1,000 MW).

segments.name: Irrigation
segments.commentary: 23% of FY26 revenue and 16% of order book; Nira Deoghar canal won at INR 958 crore total (Patel share INR 192 crore).

segments.name: Tunnelling
segments.commentary: 17% of FY26 revenue and 5% of order book; CIDCO Treated Water Tunnel recorded 812 m in one month in January 2026 and about 6.2 km tunnelled in the quarter.

segments.name: Roads, urban infra and others
segments.commentary: 5% of FY26 revenue; urban infrastructure is 10% of order book and roads and others 6%. Kondhane Dam (CIDCO, about INR 1,300 crore) is the largest FY26 win.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 10%, with momentum expected to strengthen meaningfully from H2 FY27.
FY27 new order inflow expected at around INR 8,000 crore, supported by L1 position on INR 1,600 crore (Lower Arun, Nepal).
Subansiri Lower: all eight units expected to be operational in FY27.
Non-core asset monetisation target of INR 150-200 crore in FY27 (FY26 realised about INR 185 crore).
Interest cost expected to stay broadly flat in FY27 despite debt paydown, as new project advances of INR 700-800 crore come in.
Promoter pledge reduction target of around 15-20%, timing to be confirmed after lender discussions; OCD balance of INR 100-120 crore to be repaid over FY27-FY28.
capex_capacity: Subansiri Lower: four units (1,000 MW) operational after Unit-4 commissioning; civil work completed up to Unit 6; all eight units targeted in FY27.
Kiru and Kwar HEP in J&K are at full-scale concreting.
FY26 execution: over 13.5 lakh cubic metres of concreting and about 60,000 metric tonnes of reinforcement.
Current tender pipeline: about INR 6,000 crore submitted and under evaluation; INR 20,000 crore immediate pipeline; INR 40,000 crore to be bid over the next year.
demand_pricing: FY26 order inflow about INR 4,400 crore across hydropower, urban infrastructure, irrigation and other segments; order book INR 15,119 crore at 31 Mar 2026.

Major FY26 wins: Kondhane Dam about INR 1,300 crore (CIDCO), Renuka Ji Dam package about INR 900 crore (HPPCL), NEEPCO HEO 240 MW about INR 700 crore, Teesta-V about INR 240 crore (NHPC), Dorjilung Bhutan about INR 231 crore, and two coal mining packages totalling INR 798 crore (SECL, MDO model).
Management said it lost a large hydro project (Dibang, about INR 16,000-17,000 crore) to a new player that bid very low; hydro success ratio was 12-13% including it, 25-30% excluding it.
Pipeline cited: Sawalkote 1,856 MW, Kalai-II 1,200 MW, Kamala 1,720 MW, Upper Subansiri 1,600 MW, Etalin 3,000 MW; Kamala/Lower Subansiri bids expected in about six months.

qa_highlights.question: What hydro market share did the company achieve in FY26 wins, and why was the large Dibang-type project lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a success ratio of 12-13% including the large project (about INR 16,000-17,000 crore) and 25-30% excluding it; the loss was attributed to a new bidder pricing very low.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and order outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue growth of about 10% and about INR 8,000 crore of new orders, based on the INR 1,600 crore L1 win and the INR 6,000 crore of tenders under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Why were exceptional items booked this quarter and is more pending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is nothing further pending: a INR 56 crore impairment on hydro subsidiary investments and a INR 30 crore loss on the ACP Tollways stake (sale offer INR 55 crore, 32% stake) were booked; FY25 exceptional items related to the Vivad se Vishwas settlement of about INR 150 crore.

qa_highlights.question: PAT grew about 25% against 4% revenue growth: how much is from finance costs or tax, and what is the normalized PAT growth trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance costs fell by almost Rs 10 crore YoY on lower debt and are expected to stay at a reduced level. EBITDA margin is around 13-14%, so the PAT gain is mainly from lower interest. Current-year PAT growth estimate is about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the existing order book support double-digit growth without material new wins, and what is its execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is to be executed over about 3 years, with book-to-bill around 3x. Target new order inflow is about Rs 8,000 crore this year, needed for 10% growth this year and 15% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company have any exceptional items in FY27, after about Rs 150 crore in the last two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect exceptional items this year. Last year's items were mainly Vivaad-se-Vishwas settlements and some investment write-downs.

qa_highlights.question: Details of the Telangana land sale and further monetization?
qa_highlights.answer: The sale was 27 acres for Rs 26-27 crore, leaving about 400 acres in Telangana. Other parcels are under discussion. Non-core monetization target is Rs 150-200 crore this year.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter pledge reduction timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters and the company are in talks with lenders and expect a substantial reduction this year. Management said around 85-90% of shares are pledged and expects at least a 15-20% reduction, without a specific timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Patel Smondo OC timing and occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: OC is expected this financial year after a pending litigation closes. The third tower is a service apartment tower, ready to occupy once OC comes. Some buyers have taken possession for fit-outs.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 15%, and are buybacks or ESOPs being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not confirm 15% margins because competition has risen and a large project was lost last year. Margins are targeted at 13-14%. Buybacks will be considered after debt reduction, which may take two to three years. ESOPs will be handled through the existing ESOP trust.

qa_highlights.question: How much working capital and capex will execution need, and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Client advances against bank guarantees or surety bonds should cover most needs. Working capital borrowing of Rs 100-200 crore may be needed in between. The 14.02% margin is mostly project mix, with an average of 13-14%.

qa_highlights.question: Dredging, and the arbitration awards above Rs 1,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is looking at dredging work, alone or with partners. Arbitrations are being followed up, and settlements are explored where possible. PSUs usually litigate through all courts.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and Q2 revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days are 40-45, and this continues in new contracts. Q2 is seasonally slower because of monsoon, with some ups and downs but no major disruption expected.

qa_highlights.question: Hydro bids under evaluation and outcome timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Bids under evaluation total about Rs 9,000 crore, mostly Arunachal and North-East hydro, with a Rs 60,000 crore pipeline. Management said outcomes are hoped for by Diwali, which the CEO called hopeful.

qa_highlights.question: Retention money and release timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Retention is about 5% of each contract, around Rs 200-250 crore on the balance sheet. It is mostly released at project end, though some projects allow withdrawal against bank guarantees.

531120|2026-09.headline: Patel Engineering Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue flat at INR 1211 crore; H1 PAT up 15.94% to INR 177 crore, FY27 growth guided to 7-8%.
531120|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was INR 1211 crore versus INR 1208 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA margin down to 12.42% from 13.13% and PAT up 7.64% to INR 83 crore. Management blamed uneven monsoon rain in hilly project sites and delayed new project starts pending forest clearances. Order book stood at INR 13,546 crore at September 30, 2026, and bids worth about INR 30,000 crore are pending, with management expecting most to open by March. Management cut its FY27 revenue growth expectation to roughly 7-8% from the earlier 10%, with stronger growth deferred to FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 growth will be marginal, around 7-8%. FY28 is expected to pick up as the ~INR 30,000 crore bids open and mobilise after a 6-7 month phase; FY28 visibility is limited.

qa_highlights.question: How much hydropower did the industry win in the last six months, and what did the company win in the prior year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no hydro projects were finalised in the last six months. Last year's INR 4,400 crore inflow included about INR 700 crore of hydro, with one project won out of three or four bids.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company buy back shares, or pay dividends given free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend or distribution is planned this year because capital is needed for bids that may open. Management will review next year. A buyback was not addressed beyond 'will discuss internally'.

qa_highlights.question: Will the land bank be monetised to cut debt and release pledged shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said land sales are ongoing but depend on market conditions. Over the last four to five years more than INR 1000 crore of land was sold. Promoter pledge fell from about 88-90% to 67%, and further reduction was pushed to next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will total debt rise as new projects are won?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital debt will rise with new projects, but management expects land sales and award receipts to offset this on a year-on-year basis. Some intra-year increase is possible.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TBM supply risk from China, and what about cost inflation and margin?

531201|2026-09.headline: Shilchar Q2 FY27 revenue rose 43% QoQ to INR192.61 crore with EBITDA margin at 20.8%, while FY27 INR750 crore target is reiterated.
531201|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR192.61 crore, up 43% QoQ and 12% YoY, as deferred Q1 export dispatches landed and domestic demand stayed strong. EBITDA excluding other income was INR40.06 crore (20.8% margin, up from 16.4% in Q1) and PAT was INR32.98 crore (16.5% margin). Management reiterated the FY27 revenue target of INR750 crore, with H1 sales of about INR330 crore and an order book of over INR550 crore. Margins remain below the roughly 28-30% levels of FY24-FY26, and management shifted guidance to absolute EBITDA (INR200-250 crore) rather than percentage margin.

financial_highlights.metric: Net working capital increase in H1
financial_highlights.change: includes financial assets up to about INR29 crore, per analyst

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Export mix was about 40% in Q2 and the order book is about 60:40 domestic:export. Middle East shipments were still below normal, offset partly by North America, where US tariffs were withdrawn in February. Management said export margins are higher than domestic, but did not quantify.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic demand was described as very strong throughout. Mix is mainly renewable-related transformers, with distribution transformers made in very small quantities.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR750 crore reiterated; management said it will be more than that, and analysts were told quarterly run-rate of INR225-230 crore is needed.
FY27 EBITDA target is more than INR200 crore (INR225-250 crore in absolute terms) with percentage margin unspecified; management would not give a margin number and said it is difficult to guess.
Margins expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 with about 100% capacity utilisation and more export orders.
FY28 revenue target about INR1,000 crore; FY29 target INR1,250-1,500 crore, with maximum INR1,500 crore at 100% utilisation of 14,000 MVA capacity.
Management said margins may fall as capacity grows, but targets absolute EBITDA growth; the same or higher EBITDA margin is targeted in the long term.
capex_capacity: Expansion Phase 3 adds 6,500 MVA, taking total capacity to 14,000 MVA; commissioning expected April 2027.
Civil foundation, PEB erection and utility work are in progress; all major production equipment has been ordered.
Current utilisation is about 80% of installed capacity in Q2; management expects about 100% in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Approvals for 220 kV class transformers expected 3-6 months after the new plant starts; existing customers have given verbal commitments for orders.
Management said breakeven utilisation on the new capacity is about 35-40%.
demand_pricing: Lead times: about 3-6 months for lower kV classes; more than 1 year for higher kV classes.
Raw material prices have stabilised but remain above pre-crisis levels; new orders are priced on current raw material costs. Management said the price rise was partly passed on, but not fully.
Working capital: no bank working-capital borrowing; receivables are mainly LC-backed (for example, 180-day LCs with interest borne by the customer).
Demand drivers cited: data centres, renewables, BESS, transmission and distribution. Management said capacity additions should not pressure margins for at least a couple of years.
Analyst cited raw material cost at about 71-72% of sales versus about 60% earlier; management did not dispute this.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 revenue jump came from deferred Q1 revenue, and what is the FY27 path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of Q2 came from Q1 deferrals and part from new orders. It said H2 quarterly sales should be INR225-230 crore to reach the INR750 crore target.

qa_highlights.question: How much did higher freight cut EBITDA, and can margins return to about 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: No quantification of freight impact was given. Management said margins will fall as volumes rise, but absolute EBITDA is targeted at INR225-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Are approvals in place for 220 kV transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: No approvals yet; applications follow plant commissioning, expected to take 3-6 months. Margins on 220 kV are expected to match current classes.

qa_highlights.question: Are there sustained margin outlooks (for example 23-25%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a percentage. It said it is focused on absolute EBITDA; one analyst's implied 23-24% margin was framed as 'we will be trying for that'.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakeven utilisation on the new capacity, and what is the demand risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 35-40% utilisation is breakeven and that demand is supported by power demand growth. It acknowledged a trade-off between growth and margin.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any acquisition or diversification plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is exploring options but is bound by an NDA and will disclose once progressed.

FY27 EBITDA target of INR200 crore needs about 30% margin in H2 on the management's own assumptions, while Q2 margin was 20.8%.
Heavy capacity additions industry-wide and competition from new entrants, including Waaree, may pressure pricing.
Watch for 220 kV approvals after April 2027 commissioning, Q3 revenue run-rate of INR225 crore, and the export mix improving from 40%.
Working capital rose sharply in H1, with receivables and financial assets up; management attributes this to LC-backed terms.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA target of INR200-250 crore needs about 30% margin in H2 per the brief, against Q2 margin of 20.8%, with raw material at about 71-72% of sales and Middle East freight and export volumes still below normal.

rows.why: 220 kV class transformers are planned, with approvals expected 3-6 months after the new plant starts and existing customers already giving verbal order commitments.

rows.why: US tariffs were withdrawn in February and North America is offsetting weak Middle East shipments, but export mix is about 40% and management did not quantify export margin uplift.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the order book and the INR750 crore revenue target, but declined to give margin percentages and did not quantify freight or export mix; analysts pressed on the implied margin needed for the EBITDA target, raw material cost pass-through and 220 kV approvals.

531209|2026-03.headline: Nucleus Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue INR 224.77 crore, flat YoY, while order book rose to INR 1,044.31 crore from INR 656.68 crore in December 2025.
531209|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 224.77 crore, up 2% QoQ but down 1.8% YoY, and full-year revenue rose 5.3% to INR 876.03 crore. EBITDA fell sharply to INR 34.62 crore from INR 74.33 crore a year earlier, as cost of delivery rose to 70.1% of revenue from 57.3%. Net profit was INR 34.55 crore for the quarter versus INR 64.77 crore YoY, with full-year net profit down to INR 116.74 crore from INR 163 crore. The order book closed at INR 1,044.31 crore, up sharply QoQ, though management said most of it would convert to revenue over several quarters. Management flagged the loss of Bajaj Finance to a competitor it said Bajaj had invested in, and some Middle East orders were postponed due to the war situation.

Power tillers grew about 18% and power weeders about 56% in volume, while domestic tractors grew 4.5% and tractor exports were 275 units. Management declined to give a full-year FY27 outlook, saying it would be clearer in about a month, and said the July volume softness reflected a high base.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the policy is to maximise shareholder value and it expects to deploy capital over the next 18-24 months. No development on non-core assets yet.

qa_highlights.answer: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026 is already ready. TREM 3A from April 2028 is covered. Full Stage 5 for tractors in 2032 may add 25-30% to technology cost at current prices.

531266|2026-09.headline: VST Tillers Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2% to INR321.6 crore, but operational EBITDA margin fell about 200 bps to 11% on commodity costs.

531279|2026-03.headline: Trishakti FY26 revenue rose ~90% to INR 32.44 crore, but EBITDA includes INR 4.58 crore subvention income and receivables sit near 200 days.

531279|2026-06.headline: Trishakti Q1 FY27 total income up ~310% YoY to INR 1,680 lakh, EBITDA ~INR 1,087 lakh at ~65% margin, PAT INR 430 lakh.

531279|2026-09.headline: Trishakti Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 133% YoY to INR 1,551 lakhs, with EBITDA margin of 60.89%.

H1 FY27 revenue was INR 2,989 lakhs, EBITDA INR 1,790 lakhs and PAT INR 949 lakhs. Management said about INR 370 crore of the INR 400 crore FY25-FY27 capex programme (incl. GST) is deployed, and announced "Mission 2030" targeting cumulative gross block above INR 1,000 crore by FY30. Receivable days rose over the past two years; management attributed this to a family settlement and said the cycle will normalise to about 60-65 days by year end.

qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a family settlement from three years ago that extended the cycle; about INR 75 lakh of provision was created this quarter and the cycle should return to about 60-65 days by year end. Management also said about INR 3 crore is over one year old, linked to the family settlement.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects net debt of INR 400-500 crore until FY30, funded by bank debt and internal accruals; most FY24-FY25 machines to be free of bank financing by FY28. Only fixed-rate loans apart from the CC limit, which was unused since January; 25 bps rate increase expected on new funding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on equity dilution and UAE/KSA expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is the first priority and equity dilution is a final option; it could double the fleet by next year if debt is hard to raise. UAE and KSA expansion depends on internal accruals or equity; KSA local-stake rules reportedly changed after 1 May, allowing 100% ownership.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the receivable cycle elevated, and what caused the move in other current liabilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said month-end revenue is not billed for 10-12 days because overtime is computed, so trade receivables run high; the move to monthly GST filing shifted about INR 2.5-3 crore of billing, and cash flow should improve from this quarter. Other current liabilities relate to machine funding timing.

531335|2026-03.headline: Zydus Wellness Q4 FY26 net sales grew 62.1% on Comfort Click, but net profit fell 5.8% as seasonal brands dropped 9.8% in the domestic business.

Domestic seasonal brands fell 9.8% as a delayed summer and rain in March and mid-April left retail and wholesale pipelines unfilled, while skin and hair care rose 39.7% and food and nutrition rose 9.4%. EBITDA grew 42.2% to INR 2,701 million, but net profit fell 5.8% due to higher finance costs from the acquisition debt, higher amortization of acquired brands and exceptional items. Management said operating leverage and the 17-18% EBITDA margin goal remain intact, while the seasonal recovery is expected from May onwards.

531335|2026-06.headline: Zydus Wellness Q1 FY27 consolidated net sales rose 66.7% YoY to INR 14,299 million, with EBITDA up 55.3% to INR 2,417 million, while reported net profit fell 7%.

Reported net profit declined 7%, but profit excluding amortisation of acquired brands grew 26.5%. The domestic business grew 4.6%, with Skin & Hair Care up 34.5% and Food & Nutrition up 16%, while seasonal brands fell 12% due to unseasonal rains in the East and North. International (including Comfort Click) grew 24.8% like-to-like, and management said the summer weakness was recovering in the second half of the quarter.

531335|2026-09.headline: Zydus Wellness Q2 FY27 consolidated net sales rose 74.6% YoY to INR 11,227 million, with EBITDA up 271.7% to INR 855 million.
531335|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 net sales were INR 11,227 million (+74.6% YoY) and H1 net sales were INR 25,526 million (+70.1%), with the Comfort Click acquisition inflating the inorganic growth. Domestic portfolio grew 29.2% in the quarter but only 13.3% in H1, as seasonal brands rebounded from a weak Q1. International like-to-like growth slowed to 12.4% in Q2 from 18.6% in H1, with management attributing the slowdown to a Prime Day shift, a website migration in one market and softer Amazon sales in one or two markets. Management said gross margin improved in the core business on a like-for-like basis, while sequential gross margin may look lower due to seasonal mix, and it took calibrated price increases of under 2% blended.

segments.name: Domestic portfolio
segments.commentary: Q2 growth 29.2% with seasonal brands +123.5% on low base; H1 growth 13.3% with seasonal brands -8.7%. Management said rural demand is holding and growing slightly faster than urban.

segments.name: Skin and hair care
segments.commentary: Q2 growth 37.5%, H1 35.8%; Everyuth grew at double-digit rates, Cuticolor saw strong uptake with Bright Brown launch. Management says Everyuth facial cleansing share rose from rank 7 to rank 4 in a category of about INR 4,500 crore.

segments.name: Food and Nutrition
segments.commentary: Q2 growth 25.1%, H1 20.7%. Complan posted double-digit growth for a third straight quarter; Nutralite grew strong double digits; Sugar Free grew double digits; RiteBite Max Protein sustained strong growth.

segments.name: International (Comfort Click)
segments.commentary: Like-to-like growth 12.4% in Q2 and 18.6% in H1, versus 25% growth reported last quarter per analyst. Management targets double-digit growth for H2 and states Comfort Click EBITDA margin steady state of 14-15%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit growth for Comfort Click to continue into H2 FY27, though Q2 was below its internal expectation.
Core business EBITDA margin to improve through gross margin gains and operating leverage; management says it is confident of medium-term margin expansion despite inflation.
Management intends to match or improve domestic gross margins in H2 FY27 despite the high base in H2 FY26, but said outcome is uncertain in a volatile environment.
Further calibrated price increases planned in H2, targeted at specific SKUs where commodity costs (e.g., milk, PET) rise; palm oil has stabilised.
Domestic A&P to stay at about 12.5%-13% of sales; Comfort Click A&P at 23%-24%, with stepped-up middle and top funnel spend.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.
Newly set up own medical marketing team supports direct supply for Complan NutriGro (2-6 year toddler range).
RiteBite Max Protein cookies (10 g protein, no palm oil, maida or added sugar) launched pan-India across online and offline channels.
demand_pricing: Blended price increase taken so far is less than 2%, applied only to SKUs with direct input cost impact; commodity inflation in single digits, with dextrose under annual tie-up.
Comfort Click slowdown attributed to Prime Day timing shift from June to July, a website migration in one market, and softer Amazon sales in one or two markets; management called these temporary.
Newer launches contributed about 2% of growth in the last year, with launches over 3-4 years at about 4% (per management's reply to a question).
Competitive intensity in Comfort Click is higher than expected, which management said was anticipated, and more players are entering functional snacking (RiteBite).
Complan growth attributed to celebrity campaign, 50% lower sugar relaunch and NutriGro relaunch.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Comfort Click growth slow from 25% to 12%, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a Prime Day shift from June to July, a website migration in one market and marketplace slowdowns; H1 international growth is 18%+ and double-digit growth is still targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Is Amazon slowing for Comfort Click?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one or two markets saw Amazon slowdown that it considers temporary; it is expanding to Boots and other marketplaces.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic A&P stays at about 12.5%-13% of sales; Comfort Click A&P runs at 23%-24%, and management will not cut marketing to expand EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What are Comfort Click margins and the price increases taken in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Comfort Click EBITDA margin steady state is 14-15%; management would not give brand-level margins and said price increases were calibrated and not portfolio-wide.

qa_highlights.question: Can consolidated gross margin return to the 65% range if Comfort Click growth recovers to 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it hypothetical, said the company would be in a similar zone, and said it would revert with a calculation.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Comfort Click margin pressured like-for-like given strong domestic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Comfort Click margins are holding well and that it invested in domestic brand building, which weighed on the bottom line.

risks_watch: Comfort Click growth decelerated to 12% in Q2 from 25% last quarter; H2 double-digit target depends on recovery in marketplace and website-shift markets.
Heightened competition in Comfort Click and new entrants in functional snacking (RiteBite) could pressure growth and pricing.
Commodity inflation (milk, PET, palm oil) may require further price increases and could dent consumer demand if sustained.
Sequential gross margin may look lower in Q3 due to seasonal mix; H2 faces a high base from last year's strong gross margins.
Seasonal brands (Glucon-D, Nycil) remain negative in H1 at -8.7%, and management does not disclose seasonal brand contribution.

531344|2026-03.headline: CONCOR posted record FY26 throughput of 5.58 million TEUs (+9.6%), but PAT fell 4.5% and Q4 domestic EBIT margin collapsed to 0.2%.
531344|2026-03.overview: FY26 handling hit a record 5.58 million TEUs (+9.6%), with EXIM at 8% and domestic at 14.6% growth, and rail freight margin rose to 27.16% from 25.65%. PAT declined 4.5% on weaker domestic traffic (gunny bags and Morbi tiles hit by West Asia-related supply disruptions) and tank container shortages. Q4 domestic segment EBIT margin fell to 0.2%, driven by higher empty running and a sharp rise in other expenses. Management guided FY27 handling growth of 9.5% (EXIM 8%, domestic 15%), kept EBITDA margin at 24-25%, and cited the DFC connection to JNPT from 1 June 2026 as a major driver.

segments.commentary: Q4 segment EBIT margin 0.2%, with revenue down about 4% YoY. Gunny bag (jute) and Morbi tile traffic collapsed, forcing empty container repositioning; Q4 domestic empty running rose 11.3% to INR76.76 crore. Market share fell to 55.9% from 57.6%.

segments.commentary: FY26 rail coefficient: JNPT 15.12% (CONCOR share 60%), Mundra 24.6% (share 35.4%), Pipavav 57.5% (share 48.3%). Overall market share 54.5% vs 55.9% last year.

No long-term (multi-year) volume guidance given; prior reference to 10 million TEUs by FY29-30 not reaffirmed.

demand_pricing: Management said EXIM volumes were hit in March and April 2026 by West Asia conflict, with recovery from May; no quantified June-quarter numbers given.

531344|2026-09.headline: CONCOR posted record Q2 FY27 handling of 1,448,379 TEUs and turnover of INR2,373 crore, with standalone PBT of INR462 crore despite West Asia disruption.
531344|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as decent under difficult geopolitics, with the Strait of Hormuz container traffic practically closed and trade diverted to Khor Fakkan and Fujairah. Total handling volume, operating turnover and total income were all reported as record highs for any quarter, though revenue growth was only 0.93%. Domestic volumes were weak in H1 (tiles at Morbi, gunny bags in Bengal, food grains shifting to BCN wagons) and domestic EBIT margin fell to around 2% per an analyst, which management attributed to competitive pricing and rising costs. Management refused to revise FY27 guidance, deferring it to December, and tariffs at Dadri and TKD were cut 10-20% to win modal shift.

531358|2026-09.headline: Choice International Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to Rs 379 crore and PAT rose 23% to Rs 69-70 crore, a record quarter.

The company completed a Rs 900 crore NH Investment & Securities investment in the broking arm via CCPS, announced a 1:1 bonus issue, and moved the Feedback Infra acquisition forward with a Letter of Intent from the Resolution Professional. 531431|2026-06.headline: Shakti Pumps Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37.9% YoY to INR859 crores, but EBITDA margin stayed near 9.6% on raw material and realisation pressure.
531431|2026-06.overview: Management reported a record quarterly revenue of INR859 crores (up 37.9% YoY from INR623 crores) and PAT of INR52 crores, up 35% QoQ, with PAT margin at 6% versus 4.5% in Q4 FY26. EBITDA margin was about 9.6%, which management said was broadly stable sequentially, while YoY EBITDA fell from INR144 crores to INR83 crores due to raw material inflation (about INR36 crores) and lower sales realisation (about INR25 crores). Solar pump installations rose 57.6% YoY to 27,678 units, and the order book was about INR1,000 crores as of 22 July 2026. Management reiterated a target of INR5,000 crores revenue by FY29 and tied margin recovery to PM-KUSUM 2.0 launch and easing raw material prices.

vs INR144 crores a year ago
